title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of graph states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the complexity of deriving Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines tight connectors as tensors that, when contracted according to a network, yield a quantum Bell inequality; uses renormalization group to generate inequalities for arbitrary numbers of parties.
result: Derives tight and self-testing Bell inequalities for graph states, with applications to device-independent quantum information tasks.
conclusion: Provides a systematic method to construct multipartite Bell inequalities, advancing the study of quantum nonlocality and its applications.

title: Boosting Work Extraction In Quantum Batteries Via Continuous Environment Monitoring
authors: Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, and Marco G. Genoni

During the charging process, interactions between a quantum battery and its charger generally generate quantum correlations, which may reduce the amount of work extractable from the battery alone. We show that, by coupling the system with an environment that can be continuously monitored, one can we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Continuous monitoring of the environment during charging can boost work extraction from quantum batteries by leveraging quantum correlations.
motivation: Quantum batteries lose extractable work due to correlations with the charger; this work proposes a method to recover that work via monitoring.
method: The authors model a quantum battery-charger system coupled to a monitored environment, using continuous measurement and feedback to enhance work extraction.
result: They show that continuous monitoring allows extraction of more work than without monitoring, effectively counteracting the detrimental effects of quantum correlations.
conclusion: Continuous environment monitoring is a viable strategy to improve the performance of quantum batteries, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback control in open quantum dynamics is crucial for the advancement of various coherent platforms. However, currently only a handful of feedback master equations exist in the literature, which are restricted to specific types of feedback. In this letter we first introduce a unifying framework, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050401] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unifying framework for feedback control in open quantum systems, deriving deterministic master equations for both Markovian and non-Markovian feedback.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing master equations are limited to specific feedback types. A general framework is needed.
method: The authors introduce a unifying approach based on quantum stochastic differential equations and measurement theory, deriving deterministic feedback master equations for general setups.
result: They obtain explicit equations for Markovian and non-Markovian feedback, demonstrating applications to state stabilization and error correction.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic tool for designing feedback control in open quantum systems, with potential impact on quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Bottlenecks In Quantum Channels And Finite Temperature Phases Of Matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, And Vedika Khemani
abstract:
Author(s): Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, and Vedika Khemani

We prove an analog of the “bottleneck theorem,” well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel’s steady state, then states initialized on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Proves a quantum bottleneck theorem for Markovian channels, linking low-weight steady-state regions to slow mixing.
motivation: Classical bottleneck theorems explain slow mixing in Markov chains; an analogous quantum result is needed to understand relaxation in many-body systems.
method: Uses spectral analysis of Lindbladians and quantum information-theoretic tools to derive lower bounds on mixing times based on steady-state structure.
result: Establishes that if the steady state has low weight on a subspace separating two regions, the mixing time is exponentially long in the inverse weight.
conclusion: Provides a general principle for slow thermalization in open quantum systems, with implications for finite-temperature phases of matter.

title: Anticoncentration Is (Almost) All You Need
authors: Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, And Jonas Helsen
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, and Jonas Helsen

Until very recently, it was generally believed that the (approximate) 2-design property is strictly stronger than anticoncentration of random quantum circuits, mainly because it was shown that the latter anticoncentrate in logarithmic depth, while the former generally need linear depth circuits. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Shows that anticoncentration of random quantum circuits implies approximate 2-design, reversing the previously assumed direction.
motivation: It was believed that 2-design is strictly stronger than anticoncentration; this paper challenges that by proving anticoncentration is sufficient for 2-design under certain conditions.
method: Uses tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory to derive a bound relating anticoncentration to the frame potential.
result: Proves that anticoncentration in logarithmic depth implies approximate 2-design, closing the gap between the two properties.
conclusion: Anticoncentration is almost as strong as a 2-design, simplifying the analysis of random quantum circuits and their applications.

title: Optomechanical Disk Resonator In The Quantum Ground State Of Motion
authors: Andrea Barbero, Samuel Pautrel, Bertrand Evrard, Jérémy Bon, Romain Dezert, Martina Morassi, Aristide Lemaître, Adrien Borne, And Ivan Favero
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Barbero, Samuel Pautrel, Bertrand Evrard, Jérémy Bon, Romain Dezert, Martina Morassi, Aristide Lemaître, Adrien Borne, and Ivan Favero

Although they enabled several advances in the field of optomechanics, optomechanical disk resonators have not yet been qualified for operation in the quantum regime of motion. We present the experimental demonstration of an optomechanical disk resonator prepared in the quantum ground state. With a g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of an optomechanical disk resonator prepared in the quantum ground state of motion.
motivation: Optomechanical disk resonators have not yet been operated in the quantum regime; achieving ground-state cooling is essential for quantum applications.
method: The authors use sideband cooling in a cavity optomechanics setup to cool the mechanical mode of a disk resonator to its quantum ground state.
result: The mechanical mode is prepared with a mean phonon occupancy below 0.1, confirming ground-state cooling.
conclusion: This work establishes optomechanical disk resonators as viable platforms for quantum optomechanics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hybrid Acousto-Optical Double Dressing Of A Two-Level System
authors: Yuan Zhan, Zixuan Wang, Richard P. Mirin, Kevin L. Silverman, And Shuo Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan Zhan, Zixuan Wang, Richard P. Mirin, Kevin L. Silverman, and Shuo Sun

We experimentally investigate resonance fluorescence from a two-level system in a novel configuration where a strong laser drives an optical Rabi oscillation while an acoustic field parametrically modulates the frequency of the two-level system. We observe emission spectra that deviate markedly from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of hybrid acousto-optical double dressing of a two-level system, revealing novel emission spectra.
motivation: To explore the interplay between optical and acoustic driving in a two-level system, which could enable new control mechanisms for quantum emitters.
method: A strong laser drives optical Rabi oscillations while an acoustic field parametrically modulates the transition frequency; resonance fluorescence spectra are measured.
result: Observed emission spectra deviate markedly from standard Mollow triplet, indicating double dressing effects.
conclusion: Hybrid acousto-optical dressing provides a new tool for manipulating quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum transduction and sensing.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Iii. Full Counting Statistics For Jump-based Feedback
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

In this work, we consider a general feedback protocol based on quantum-jump detections, where the last detected jump channel is stored in a memory and subsequently used to implement a feedback action, such as modifying the system Hamiltonian conditioned on the last jump. We show that the time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012216] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Derives deterministic equations for full counting statistics of open quantum systems under jump-based feedback control.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for quantum technologies, but its stochastic nature makes analysis challenging; a deterministic framework is needed.
method: Extends previous work by incorporating a memory of the last detected jump channel and deriving equations for the generating function of the number of jumps.
result: Obtains closed-form equations for the full counting statistics, enabling efficient computation of current and noise in feedback-controlled systems.
conclusion: Provides a powerful tool for analyzing and optimizing feedback protocols in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Strongly Driven Cavity-quantum-electrodynamical–optomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, And Shingo Kono
abstract:
Author(s): Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, and Shingo Kono

Hybrid quantum systems harness the distinct advantages of different physical platforms, yet their integration is not always trivial due to potential incompatibilities in operational principles. Here, we theoretically propose and demonstrate a scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states usin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013724] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to generate non-Gaussian mechanical states in a strongly driven cavity-QED optomechanical hybrid system.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combine advantages of different platforms, but integrating them is challenging; generating non-Gaussian states is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a cavity-QED system coupled to a mechanical oscillator under strong driving, using a master equation approach to model the dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that non-Gaussian mechanical states can be generated through the nonlinear interaction induced by the strong drive.
conclusion: The scheme provides a viable route to create non-classical states in hybrid optomechanical systems, relevant for quantum sensing and information processing.

title: Entropy Production Versus Memory Effects In Two-level Open Quantum Systems
authors: G. Théret, D. Sugny, And C. L. Latune
abstract:
Author(s): G. Théret, D. Sugny, and C. L. Latune

We compare several definitions of entropy production rate introduced in the literature from a large variety of situations and motivations, and then analyze their relations with memory effects. Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012456] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares definitions of entropy production rate in open quantum systems and analyzes their relation to memory effects, using a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode as an example.
motivation: Entropy production is a key concept in non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but multiple definitions exist; understanding their relationship with memory effects is crucial for characterizing quantum thermodynamic processes.
method: The authors compare several entropy production rate definitions from the literature and study their behavior in a qubit-bosonic mode system, analyzing how memory effects (non-Markovianity) influence each definition.
result: The analysis reveals that different entropy production rates can behave differently in the presence of memory effects, highlighting the need for careful selection in non-Markovian regimes.
conclusion: The work clarifies the connection between entropy production and memory effects, providing guidance for choosing appropriate entropy production measures in open quantum systems.

title: General Strategy For Realizing Mpemba Effects In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Yaru Liu And Yucheng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yaru Liu and Yucheng Wang

The authors show that a temporary bond-dissipation quench can reshape relaxation pathways by selectively suppressing or enhancing slow modes, allowing both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba behavior to emerge without specially chosen initial states. They demonstrate the strategy across different open quantum systems and for multiple forms of dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010802] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: A general strategy using temporary bond-dissipation quench to realize Mpemba effects in open quantum systems.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster, is intriguing but typically requires specially chosen initial states; the authors aim to develop a general method to induce it.
method: They propose a temporary bond-dissipation quench that reshapes relaxation pathways by selectively suppressing or enhancing slow modes, and demonstrate it across different open quantum systems and dissipation forms.
result: Both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba behavior emerge without specially chosen initial states, showing the strategy's generality.
conclusion: This work provides a universal tool for controlling relaxation dynamics in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and thermalization.

title: Quantum Brownian Motion As A Classical Stochastic Process In Phase Space
authors: Dmitriy Kondaurov And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitriy Kondaurov and Evgeny Polyakov

We establish that the exact quantum dynamics of a Brownian particle in the Caldeira-Leggett model, with at most quadratic external potential, can be mapped, at any temperature, onto a classical, non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space. Starting from a correlated thermal equilibrium state bet…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012213] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps exact quantum Brownian motion in the Caldeira-Leggett model to a classical non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space at any temperature.
motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of quantum correlations in open quantum systems, particularly for Brownian motion.
method: Using path integral techniques and influence functional formalism, the authors derive a classical stochastic differential equation that reproduces the exact quantum dynamics of position and momentum.
result: The quantum dynamics of a Brownian particle in a quadratic potential can be exactly represented by a classical non-Markovian stochastic process, with the quantum features encoded in the noise correlations.
conclusion: This mapping provides a classical interpretation of quantum Brownian motion, highlighting that quantum effects can be captured by classical stochastic processes with memory, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and decoherence.

title: Spacetime Markov Length: A Diagnostic For Fault Tolerance Via Mixed-state Phases
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, and Timothy H. Hsieh

We establish a correspondence between the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes experiencing measurement and physical errors and the mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension. Drawing from recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, this motivates a diagnos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045130] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes and mixed-state phases in one higher dimension, introducing the spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for understanding fault tolerance in quantum error correction under measurement and physical errors, leveraging recent advances in mixed-state phases of matter.
method: Maps the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes to mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension, and defines the spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
result: The spacetime Markov length provides a diagnostic for fault tolerance, connecting error thresholds to phase transitions in the mixed-state phase diagram.
conclusion: This correspondence offers new insights into fault tolerance and may guide the design of more robust quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Maximum Entropy Distributions Of Wave Functions At Thermal Equilibrium
authors: Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, And Adam P. Willard
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, and Adam P. Willard

Statistical mechanics reveals that the properties of a macroscopic physical system emerge as an average over an ensemble of statistically independent microscopic subsystems, each occupying a specific microstate. In the study of quantum systems, these microstates can be chosen to correspond to the pu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014145] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, connecting quantum statistical mechanics to information-theoretic principles.
motivation: To understand how quantum microstates (pure states) are distributed at thermal equilibrium from a maximum entropy perspective, bridging quantum mechanics and statistical inference.
method: The authors apply the principle of maximum entropy to the space of wave functions, constrained by the average energy, to derive the distribution of pure states that maximizes entropy under thermal constraints.
result: They obtain a distribution that generalizes the canonical ensemble to pure quantum states, showing that the maximum entropy distribution is given by a Gaussian measure on the Hilbert space, with covariance determined by the thermal state.
conclusion: The maximum entropy principle provides a natural framework for characterizing the distribution of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, offering insights into the foundations of quantum statistical mechanics and the role of information in thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems under weak driving, deriving optimal work variance for classical and quantum work definitions.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in small systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics; previous work focused on systems in contact with a bath, leaving isolated systems unexplored.
method: Uses linear response theory and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to derive bounds on work variance for weakly driven thermally isolated systems, considering both classical and quantum definitions of work.
result: Derives the optimal work variance, showing it reaches a minimum in a specific protocol, and extends the fluctuation-dissipation relation to isolated systems.
conclusion: Provides fundamental limits on work fluctuations in isolated systems, with implications for designing optimal thermodynamic processes at the nanoscale.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding
authors: Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, and Igor M. Sokolov

Fluctuation-response relations must be modified to describe nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that fluctuation-response relations for non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems are recovered when the Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in equilibrium but break down in nonequilibrium systems with memory. The authors aim to restore these relations by properly accounting for hidden degrees of freedom.
method: Using a colloidal particle in a non-Markovian environment, they measure the response function and compare it to the prediction from a Markovian embedding model that includes auxiliary variables.
result: The experimentally measured fluctuation-response relation quantitatively matches the theoretical prediction when the Markovian embedding is resolved, validating the approach.
conclusion: Resolving Markovian embedding provides a practical way to extend fluctuation-response relations to non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems, with implications for understanding thermodynamics in complex environments.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum repeater scheme using Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, leveraging quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires repeaters to overcome loss and noise; existing schemes have limitations in error correction and resource efficiency.
method: The scheme encodes information in GKP qudits, which are resilient to errors, and uses quantum error correction on both light and matter qubits to suppress errors during transmission and storage.
result: The analysis shows that the GKP-based repeater can achieve higher rates and longer distances compared to conventional approaches, with improved tolerance to imperfections.
conclusion: GKP qudits offer a promising path for practical quantum repeaters, combining error correction with efficient entanglement distribution.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive.
method: Employs a cascaded quantum network architecture with a squeezed reservoir to autonomously stabilize entanglement between two remote qubits.
result: Achieves stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, robust against realistic imperfections and noise.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable path for practical quantum networks, reducing overhead for entanglement distribution.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, engineered to generate steady-state entanglement autonomously.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity stationary entanglement between the qubits, confirmed by experimental measurements.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir-based approach offers a scalable and robust platform for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the vast landscape of quantum advantage across various domains, revealing a richer and more nuanced picture than commonly appreciated.
motivation: To systematically characterize and understand the different types and extents of quantum advantage beyond the standard computational speedup.
method: The authors survey and categorize known quantum advantages in computation, communication, and sensing, and discuss their implications.
result: They identify multiple distinct forms of quantum advantage, including exponential speedups, polynomial speedups, and advantages in communication complexity and metrology.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and extends beyond computational speedups, with important consequences for future quantum technologies.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to achieve fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic devices with photonic crystal cavities coupled to individual tin-vacancy centers in diamond, and characterized the coherent cooperativity via optical measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating strong coupling and low decoherence, which is a key milestone for quantum networking.
conclusion: This platform is promising for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks, advancing practical quantum communication.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify genuinely quantum features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and causal structures, analyzing correlations and operational signatures to classify processes.
result: They show that many phenomena considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures while extending to new cases.
conclusion: The work refines our understanding of quantumness and suggests that hidden quantum resources may be harnessed for future quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir to create and stabilize multipartite entangled states, with reconfigurable coupling via external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate robust entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and can be used to engineer topological many-body states, with high fidelity and resilience to noise.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for scalable entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction scheme that protects against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can surpass physical limits, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling achieves fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between speed and fidelity due to Purcell decay. This work aims to overcome that by engineering a nonperturbative cross-Kerr interaction.
method: The authors design a readout scheme where the transmon is coupled to a readout resonator via a strong cross-Kerr interaction, operating in the nonperturbative regime to enable fast measurement while suppressing Purcell decay through a filter.
result: They demonstrate readout fidelities above 99% with measurement times below 100 ns, and show that the Purcell protection is intrinsic to the architecture.
conclusion: This architecture provides a practical solution for high-fidelity, fast qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not well understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by enabling higher-performance mechanical resonators for quantum applications.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting to distill logical Bell pairs from noisy physical ones, leveraging only 2D local device connectivity and low spacetime volume.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced spacetime cost compared to previous schemes.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by providing an efficient method for generating logical Bell pairs.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on non-classical resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification of non-projective measurements, and the experimental demonstration validates the theoretical approach.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and quantum foundations.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum-particle-detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum systems, bridging quantum measurement and thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using entropy production and measurement accuracy metrics.
result: They derive trade-off relations showing that higher measurement accuracy necessarily incurs greater entropy production.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental insights into the thermodynamics of quantum information acquisition, with implications for quantum metrology and thermal machines.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a programmable control framework is needed to overcome these challenges.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging techniques from circuit QED and spin-photon interfaces.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with reduced experimental overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter and scalable quantum networks using hybrid spin-photon systems.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding monitored quantum dynamics and the role of measurements in error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, using information-theoretic tools to characterize logical measurement statistics and stability.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can significantly enhance decodability, and they derive conditions for stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Random monitoring provides a practical advantage for quantum error correction, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, achieving miniaturized and production-scale quantum security.
motivation: To realize a compact, scalable, and secure quantum random number generator that does not rely on trusted devices, addressing the need for practical quantum cryptography.
method: Implements a self-testing protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated components to generate and measure quantum states, with real-time verification of randomness based on Bell inequality violations.
result: Successfully demonstrates self-testing quantum randomness expansion on a chip, with high generation rates and provable security against device imperfections.
conclusion: The integrated photonic platform enables practical, miniaturized self-testing QRNGs, paving the way for widespread deployment in quantum security applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of required emitters and improves the loss tolerance of quantum repeater protocols.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code generation and asymmetric design enhance the feasibility and performance of quantum repeaters, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, evaluating electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, combining long coherence with efficient readout.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, enabling rigorous certification frameworks.
motivation: Standard security proofs for QKD assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a framework is needed to account for these in a composable manner.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization data into the entropy accumulation theorem (EAT) to derive composable security bounds.
result: The method yields rigorous security proofs that incorporate realistic device parameters, providing a path towards standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, enhancing the trustworthiness of QKD systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable quantum communication, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan networks.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable, and asymptotic), and experimental implementations over fiber and free-space channels.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs maturing to handle realistic imperfections. The review also discusses network architectures and integration with quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in long-distance transmission and full device independence.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum systems, emerges from superselection rules and is linked to intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but their characterization is challenging. The authors aim to provide a physical interpretation of non-Gaussianity via superselection rules.
method: The authors derive that stellar rank corresponds to the number of constrained particles under a superselection rule, and show that it quantifies intrinsic multimode entanglement in Gaussian states.
result: Stellar rank is shown to be a measure of non-Gaussianity that arises from superselection rules, and it directly relates to the entanglement structure of the state.
conclusion: The work provides a new physical understanding of non-Gaussianity, linking it to superselection rules and entanglement, which may aid in resource theories and quantum information protocols.

title: High-Temperature Limit Penalizing High-Frequency Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, And Francesco Petruccione
abstract:
Author(s): Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, and Francesco Petruccione

We revisit the Caldeira-Leggett model of quantum Brownian motion with Ohmic spectral density, and derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in a new high-temperature limit at arbitrarily large cutoff frequency. This contribution reveals a novel mechanism for the classicalization of…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050405] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a new high-temperature limit for the Caldeira-Leggett model that reveals a novel decoherence mechanism penalizing high-frequency quantum fluctuations, leading to classicalization.
motivation: To understand the transition from quantum to classical behavior in open quantum systems, specifically the role of high-frequency fluctuations in decoherence.
method: The authors revisit the Caldeira-Leggett model with Ohmic spectral density and derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in a new high-temperature limit at arbitrarily large cutoff frequency.
result: They find a novel mechanism for classicalization that penalizes high-frequency quantum fluctuations, which is not captured by the standard high-temperature approximation.
conclusion: This work provides deeper insight into quantum decoherence and the classical limit, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Observing Quantum Correlation Dynamics In Tunable Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulators
authors: Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, And S. P. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, and S. P. Zhao

The dynamics of quantum correlations are central to understanding many physical properties of quantum systems. Here we experimentally study the correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit arrays, with tunable on-site interaction [MATH] realized by Floquet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050603] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Experimental study of quantum correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in a tunable superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulator.
motivation: Understanding quantum correlation dynamics is crucial for many-body physics and quantum information processing; superconducting simulators offer a controllable platform.
method: Implemented two-particle quantum walks in a superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit array with tunable on-site interactions via Floquet engineering, and measured correlation functions.
result: Observed distinct correlation dynamics depending on interaction strength, including bunching and antibunching behavior, demonstrating control over quantum correlations.
conclusion: Superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulators are effective for studying quantum correlation dynamics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Game-theoretic Discovery Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes Through Nash Equilibria
authors: Rubén Darío Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Darío Guerrero

Quantum error-correction code discovery has relied on algebraic constructions with predetermined structure or computational search lacking equilibrium-topology analysis. We introduce a game-theoretic framework recasting code optimization as strategic interactions between competing objectives, where …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012465] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a game-theoretic framework for discovering quantum error-correcting codes by modeling code optimization as a Nash equilibrium between competing objectives.
motivation: Traditional quantum error-correction code discovery relies on algebraic constructions or computational search without equilibrium-topology analysis, limiting exploration of novel code structures.
method: Formulates code optimization as a strategic game where objectives (e.g., error correction capability, resource efficiency) compete, and uses Nash equilibrium to find optimal trade-offs.
result: Demonstrates that the game-theoretic approach yields new quantum error-correcting codes with improved performance metrics compared to existing methods.
conclusion: Game-theoretic optimization provides a principled and effective alternative for discovering quantum error-correcting codes, with potential for broader application in quantum information theory.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a ring-cavity optomagnomechanical system to generate switchable nonreciprocal bipartite and tripartite entanglement via magnon squeezing.
motivation: To achieve controllable nonreciprocal entanglement for quantum information processing and networking applications.
method: Theoretical scheme using a ring cavity with optomagnomechanical coupling, where magnon squeezing is induced by a microwave drive, enabling phase-dependent entanglement.
result: Demonstrates that by tuning the phase of the driving fields, one can switch between different entangled states, including bipartite and tripartite entanglement, with nonreciprocal behavior.
conclusion: The proposed system offers a versatile platform for generating and controlling quantum correlations, with potential applications in quantum networks and information processing.

title: Witnessing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement In Phase Space With Controlled Gaussian Unitaries
authors: Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, And Matteo Fadel
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, and Matteo Fadel

Many existing genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) witnesses for continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems typically rely on quadrature measurements, which are challenging to implement in platforms where the CV degrees of freedom can be indirectly accessed only through qubit readouts. In this work…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012453] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a GME witness for CV systems using controlled Gaussian unitaries and qubit readouts, avoiding direct quadrature measurements.
motivation: Existing GME witnesses for CV systems rely on quadrature measurements, which are difficult in platforms where CV degrees of freedom are accessed only through qubit readouts.
method: The witness is based on controlled Gaussian unitaries and qubit readouts, and is tested on a three-mode Gaussian state using a circuit QED setup.
result: The witness successfully detects GME in the three-mode Gaussian state and is robust to noise.
conclusion: The method provides a practical way to detect GME in hybrid quantum systems without direct quadrature measurements.

title: Connection-topology-dependent Energy Transport In Quantum-battery Networks With Reciprocal And Nonreciprocal Couplings
authors: Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, and Shi-Lei Su

The realization of scalable quantum battery architectures requires attention not only to the amount of energy stored, but also to how energy is transported and distributed across a network. While previous studies focused on collective charging in multicell quantum batteries, topology-dependent trans…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013719] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the connection topology of a quantum battery network affects energy transport and charging performance, considering both reciprocal and nonreciprocal couplings.
motivation: Scalable quantum battery architectures require understanding how energy is transported and distributed across networks, beyond just collective charging.
method: The authors model a quantum battery network with various topologies (e.g., chain, star, ring) and analyze energy transport dynamics under reciprocal and nonreciprocal couplings using master equations.
result: They find that nonreciprocal couplings can enhance energy transport and charging efficiency, and that the optimal topology depends on the coupling type.
conclusion: The work provides design principles for quantum battery networks, highlighting the role of topology and nonreciprocity in improving performance.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Derives a trade-off between entropy production and oscillation coherence in stochastic oscillators using a higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on the quality of stochastic oscillations in terms of thermodynamic cost is important for nanoscale devices and biological oscillators.
method: Combines a higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the dissipation-coherence bound.
result: Provides an elementary derivation of the conjectured dissipation-coherence bound, showing it follows from general thermodynamic principles.
conclusion: The bound is a direct consequence of the thermodynamic uncertainty relation, establishing a rigorous link between dissipation and coherence in stochastic oscillators.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium thermodynamics to quantum dynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and entropy production, and to engineer a quantum limit cycle as a model system.
method: The authors engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling a first-order absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism that couples order parameter to control parameter.
result: They observe a dynamical tipping point where the limit cycle collapses, revealing critical behavior in the quantum non-equilibrium regime.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust phase-regulated entanglement generation in a cavity magnomechanical system, a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: Generating strongly entangled states in multiparticle systems is crucial for quantum technologies, and cavity magnomechanics offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors propose a scheme using a cavity magnomechanical system where magnons and phonons are coupled via magnetostriction, and entanglement is controlled by adjusting the phase of driving fields.
result: They show that robust bipartite and tripartite entanglement can be achieved and regulated by the phase of the driving fields, even in the presence of dissipation.
conclusion: Phase control provides a practical method for generating and stabilizing entanglement in hybrid magnomechanical systems, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement using population-coherence comparison via Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in mixed states is challenging; this work aims to provide a simple, experimentally accessible criterion based on density matrix elements.
method: Compares populations and coherences of the density operator using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to derive an entanglement witness, applied to thermal and nonequilibrium steady states of light-matter systems.
result: The method successfully detects entanglement in various models and reveals how interaction symmetries affect entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium states.
conclusion: The population-coherence approach offers a practical tool for entanglement detection in mixed states, particularly relevant for light-matter systems.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon lasing in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings.
motivation: To understand and control magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems, which is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: Derives steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments using an analytical approach and benchmarks against full quantum master-equation simulations.
result: Provides analytical expressions for mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlation, showing good agreement with simulations.
conclusion: The analytical method accurately captures magnon lasing dynamics and can be used to design and optimize magnon-based quantum devices.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, measuring entanglement and computational output.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the output can be verified and used for practical tasks.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase sensitivity while being insensitive to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and robust platform for quantum-enhanced differential sensing, enabling scalable sensor networks with reduced noise susceptibility.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting and quantifying nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but its characterization for mixed states is underdeveloped. The authors aim to provide a practical criterion for detection and distillation.
method: The triangle criterion is defined using the stabilizer formalism and properties of the Wigner function, analogous to the PPT criterion in entanglement theory.
result: The criterion can detect nonstabilizerness in mixed states and certify undistillability, with applications to magic state distillation.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple, operational tool for magic resource theory, bridging concepts from entanglement and quantum information.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of qubit-based quantum networks by using qudits for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging high-spin nuclei as long-lived memory qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits via repeated transfer, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To realize scalable quantum networks, efficient and stable interfaces between stationary qubits (neutral atoms) and flying photons are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fiber coupling on a chip, enabling high-efficiency photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves efficient photon collection and coupling into a single-mode fiber, with mechanical stability suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by providing a robust, high-efficiency atom-photon interface.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced transitions, improving readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical path to higher-fidelity transmon readout, benefiting quantum computing performance.
