title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration is crucial for quantum advantage experiments and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise was not universally characterized.
method: The authors analyze noisy random circuits using statistical mechanics mappings and derive universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of depth and noise rate.
result: They identify three depth regimes (short, intermediate, long) where anticoncentration exhibits universal behavior independent of circuit architecture, with noise suppressing anticoncentration at large depths.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, guiding experimental implementations and theoretical understanding of quantum advantage.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a theoretical framework linking it to state compression and measurement complexity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a well-defined monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the resources required for non-Gaussian state preparation and tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful tool for characterizing non-Gaussian resources in continuous-variable quantum information, with implications for quantum computing and communication.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of spectral diffusion is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, measuring spectral jumps and correlating them with environmental factors such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions.
result: They identify two main sources of spectral instability: electric field noise from nearby charge traps and phonon-induced dephasing. They demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and applying electric field stabilization can reduce spectral diffusion by an order of magnitude.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, provided that charge noise and phonon effects are mitigated. This work advances the platform for scalable quantum repeaters.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling of quantum Fisher information and critical exponents.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensors can surpass the standard quantum limit and approach the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust path to ultra-sensitive metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Quantum control protocols often suffer from low fidelity due to non-adiabatic transitions; counterdiabatic driving can suppress these but is hard to implement exactly.
method: The authors propose a variational approach to approximate counterdiabatic driving by minimizing a weighted action, using computer algebra to derive optimal control fields.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical and effective upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could constrain theories of gravity by testing whether gravity can entangle quantum systems.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete way to probe the quantum nature of gravity through laboratory experiments, with GIE as a key signature.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not provide a scalable advantage for quantum computation due to complexity-theoretic limitations.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum systems have been claimed to offer advantages in metrology and entanglement generation, but their potential for scalable quantum computation was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of simulating non-Hermitian dynamics and prove that any advantage is not scalable under standard complexity assumptions.
result: They demonstrate that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics are unlikely to yield exponential speedups for quantum computation, and that their simulation is generally hard.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian advantages are not scalable for quantum computation, aligning with the broader understanding of quantum computational complexity.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The authors categorize quantum cryptographic primitives, explain their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review systematically covers primitives such as quantum money, quantum digital signatures, quantum secret sharing, and quantum oblivious transfer, highlighting both theoretical capabilities and practical challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face significant implementation hurdles; photonic techniques are a promising avenue for experimental progress.

title: Excitable Quantum Systems: The Bosonic Avalanche Laser
authors: Louis Garbe And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Louis Garbe and Peter Rabl

We investigate the dynamics of a lasing system driven by a current of bosonic (quasi-)particles via a dissipative three-mode mixing process. A semiclassical analysis of this system predicts distinct dynamical regimes, where both the cavity mode and the gain medium can undergo lasing transitions. Of …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013723] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a bosonic avalanche laser driven by a current of bosonic particles, revealing distinct lasing regimes and non-equilibrium phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of bosonic systems driven by particle currents is important for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: A semiclassical analysis is performed on a three-mode mixing process to derive the system's dynamics and identify lasing transitions.
result: Both the cavity mode and the gain medium can undergo lasing transitions, with distinct dynamical regimes characterized by different emission properties.
conclusion: The bosonic avalanche laser provides a new platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and may have applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Correlated Steady States Under Competing Collective And Individual Decay
authors: Nikita Leppenen And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Leppenen and Ephraim Shahmoon

Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, while ubiquitous individual decay destroys them. We study the interplay between these two competing processes considering a driven system of many spins (“atoms”) undergoing both collective and individual dissipation (“radiation”). In t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013720] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between collective and individual dissipation in a driven spin system, showing that steady-state quantum correlations can be enhanced by balancing these competing processes.
motivation: Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them; understanding their competition is crucial for quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system undergoing both collective and individual dissipation using master equation techniques and derive conditions for steady-state entanglement and squeezing.
result: They find that steady-state quantum correlations, such as entanglement and spin squeezing, can persist even in the presence of strong individual decay when the collective dissipation is sufficiently strong and the driving is tuned appropriately.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that competing dissipation channels can be harnessed to produce robust quantum correlations, offering insights for quantum state preparation in open systems.

title: Emergence Of Quorum Sensing In A Cavity-coupled multi-YIG System
authors: Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, And Xiao-Hong Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, and Xiao-Hong Yan

Quorum sensing, defined as the emergence of collective behavior triggered by a critical population size or density, is a hallmark of collective biological behavior. However, it has not yet been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms. Here, we report the theoretical predictio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014425] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically predicts the emergence of quorum sensing, a collective behavior triggered by a critical number of spins, in a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system.
motivation: Quorum sensing is a hallmark of collective biological behavior but has not been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms. The authors aim to demonstrate this phenomenon in a hybrid quantum system.
method: The authors model a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system where multiple yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres are coupled to a microwave cavity. They analyze the collective dynamics and show that above a critical number of YIG spheres, a phase transition occurs leading to synchronized behavior analogous to quorum sensing.
result: The system exhibits a sharp transition to collective behavior when the number of YIG spheres exceeds a threshold, characterized by enhanced cavity transmission and spin-spin correlations.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical platform for realizing quorum sensing in a controlled quantum system, opening avenues for studying collective phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Period Doubling And Higher Multiplicities In A Driven Single-spin System
authors: Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, And Joachim Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, and Joachim Ankerhold

An individual spin-1/2 realized by a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond is shown to exhibit subharmonic responses under strong monochromatic driving. Theoretical modeling of the driven nitrogen-vacancy dynamics and stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032011] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Observation of period doubling and higher subharmonic responses in a driven NV center in diamond.
motivation: To explore nonlinear dynamics and subharmonic generation in a single-spin system under strong driving.
method: Theoretical modeling of driven NV dynamics combined with stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements.
result: Period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling are observed in the NV center's response.
conclusion: Single-spin systems can exhibit rich subharmonic behavior, relevant for quantum control and sensing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: To observe and characterize synchronization in the quantum regime, which is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics and has implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and the synchronized state is detected through joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of phase-locking and frequency entrainment between the two quantum oscillators, matching theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: Quantum synchronization is experimentally realizable and can be controlled via dissipation engineering, opening avenues for studying quantum nonlinear dynamics and potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over the ion's motional state to engineer arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states via a sequence of laser pulses.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable, limiting practical deployment.
method: The authors combine discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization.
result: They achieve secret key rates exceeding 1 Mbps over 50 km fiber and 10 kbps over 100 km, with rigorous composable security.
conclusion: This work makes high-speed, secure quantum key distribution over fiber more practical, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world implementation.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local, nondestructive readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but efficient loading and imaging without atom loss remain challenging. EIT offers a solution for continuous operation.
method: The authors apply electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading, enabling continuous operation of neutral-atom arrays with reduced atom loss.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques significantly improve the practicality of neutral-atom arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for scalable quantum computing and simulation.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging and essential for quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The framework yields high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating improved performance over existing approaches.
conclusion: The optimized multiqubit gates enable practical quantum error correction in neutral-atom systems, advancing the viability of these platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to concepts like criticality and topological order.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory on nonequilibrium quantum phases.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for spin qubits in quantum technologies, and reliable predictions of decoherence are needed to guide experimental design.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing challenges from higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for complex environments.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly predictive for spin qubit decoherence, aiding the development of quantum technologies.

title: Topological Robustness Of Orbital Angular Momentum Entanglement In Stochastic Channels
authors: Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, And Andrew Forbes
abstract:
Author(s): Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, and Andrew Forbes

Orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement gives access to multiple qubit and high dimensional Hilbert spaces but is unfortunately susceptible to disturbance, decaying in real-world noisy channels. Here, we show that an underlying topology arising from OAM entanglement remains robust to such channe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement exhibits topological robustness in stochastic channels, preserving high-dimensional entanglement despite environmental noise.
motivation: OAM entanglement is promising for high-dimensional quantum information but degrades in noisy channels; understanding its robustness is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally study OAM entanglement in stochastic channels, analyzing the topological features that protect entanglement from decay.
result: They find that the underlying topology of OAM entanglement remains robust, maintaining high-dimensional entanglement even when the quantum state is disturbed.
conclusion: Topological protection can mitigate noise effects in OAM-based quantum communication, offering a pathway to robust high-dimensional quantum information processing.

title: Levitated Nano-accelerometer Sensitized By Quantum Quench
authors: M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, And K. Aikawa
abstract:
Author(s): M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, and K. Aikawa

We realize a nanoscale accelerometer with a levitated nanoparticle near the ground state, exploiting its dynamical behavior triggered by the abrupt quench of its trapping potential. We find that rapid quenching provides a readout time at which the sensitivity is enhanced by 2 orders of magnitude wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050801] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A levitated nanoparticle near ground state is used as a nanoscale accelerometer with sensitivity enhanced by two orders of magnitude via a quantum quench.
motivation: To realize a highly sensitive nanoscale accelerometer by exploiting quantum effects in a levitated nanoparticle.
method: The trapping potential of a levitated nanoparticle is abruptly quenched, and the resulting dynamical behavior is used to read out acceleration.
result: Rapid quenching provides a readout time at which sensitivity is enhanced by two orders of magnitude compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: Quantum quench in levitated nanoparticles offers a promising route to ultra-sensitive accelerometry at the nanoscale.

title: Imperfect Blockade In Rydberg Superatoms
authors: Valentin Magro, Sébastien Garcia, And Alexei Ourjoumtsev
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Magro, Sébastien Garcia, and Alexei Ourjoumtsev

A theory of imperfect Rydberg blockade is developed and experimentally verified, promising higher-quality elements for quantum technologies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053605] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Develops and experimentally verifies a theory of imperfect Rydberg blockade in superatoms, improving quantum technology elements.
motivation: Rydberg blockade is key for quantum gates and entanglement, but imperfections limit performance; a quantitative theory is needed.
method: Combines theoretical modeling of imperfect blockade with experimental measurements on Rydberg superatoms.
result: Provides a validated theory that accounts for imperfections, enabling higher-quality quantum operations.
conclusion: The work advances practical Rydberg-based quantum technologies by understanding and mitigating blockade errors.

title: Quantum Scrambling Born Machine
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

We propose a quantum scrambling Born machine (QSBM) that decouples entanglement generation from the trainable degrees of freedom: a fixed, nontrainable scrambling unitary provides multiqubit entanglement while only single-qubit rotations are optimized. We consider three entangling unitaries (a Haar …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012464] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum scrambling Born machine that uses fixed scrambling unitaries for entanglement and optimizes only single-qubit rotations.
motivation: To simplify training of quantum generative models by decoupling entanglement generation from trainable parameters.
method: Uses a fixed, nontrainable scrambling unitary (e.g., Haar random, Clifford, or Hamiltonian evolution) to generate multiqubit entanglement, while only single-qubit rotations are optimized via gradient-based methods.
result: Demonstrates that the QSBM can learn target probability distributions with high fidelity, and the choice of scrambling unitary affects performance.
conclusion: The QSBM provides a resource-efficient approach to quantum generative modeling by reducing the number of trainable parameters while maintaining expressivity.

title: Quantum Optimal Control Of $\mathrm{Λ}$-system Ensembles
authors: Julia Cen And Domenico D'alessandro
abstract:
Author(s): Julia Cen and Domenico D'Alessandro

The quantum [MATH] system is a ubiquitous structure in many quantum technologies, where two stable, lower-energy levels are coupled indirectly via an unstable, higher-energy level that is much more susceptible to decoherence and relaxation. In this paper, we solve the problem of finding a cont…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012623] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum optimal control problem for Λ-system ensembles, providing explicit control laws to transfer population between ground states while minimizing excitation of the unstable excited state.
motivation: Λ-systems are ubiquitous in quantum technologies but suffer from decoherence in the excited state; optimal control can mitigate this by avoiding population of the excited state.
method: The authors formulate the control problem using Lie group theory and Pontryagin's maximum principle, deriving analytic solutions for the control fields that achieve population transfer with minimal excited-state population.
result: Explicit control laws are obtained that transfer population between the two ground states while keeping the excited state population arbitrarily small, with performance bounds derived.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for high-fidelity control of Λ-systems, relevant for quantum memory and transduction applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Quantum Randomness Generation And Key Distribution With Entangled Photons
authors: Hammad Anwer, Nassim Ahmed Mahammedi, Sadiq Muhammad, Piotr Mironowicz, And Mohamed Bourennane
abstract:
Author(s): Hammad Anwer, Nassim Ahmed Mahammedi, Sadiq Muhammad, Piotr Mironowicz, and Mohamed Bourennane

Quantum technologies provide solutions for information processing tasks that are not achievable with classical methods. Basic resources like the creation of private and unexpected random numbers or a secure key that is shared between two parties are examples of these capabilities. However, estimatin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012622] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of quantum random number generation and quantum key distribution using entangled photons.
motivation: To demonstrate practical quantum technologies for generating private random numbers and secure keys using entangled photon pairs.
method: Uses a source of polarization-entangled photons and performs measurements to extract randomness and establish a shared secret key between two parties.
result: Successfully generates quantum random numbers and distributes a secure key, validating the feasibility of entanglement-based quantum communication.
conclusion: Entangled photon sources are viable for both quantum randomness generation and quantum key distribution, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Scalable High-fidelity And Near-deterministic Preparation Of Large-photon-number States
authors: Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, And Ming Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, and Ming Xue

The scalable preparation of large photon-number (Fock) states is a long-standing frontier in quantum science, with direct implications for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing. Despite substantial progress at small photon numbers, extending state generation to large photon nu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013721] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: A scalable method for preparing large-photon-number Fock states with high fidelity and near-deterministic success, using a hybrid system of superconducting qubits and microwave cavities.
motivation: Large Fock states are crucial for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited to small photon numbers.
method: The protocol uses a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a microwave cavity, employing a sequence of qubit rotations and cavity displacements to iteratively build up the Fock state.
result: Numerical simulations show that Fock states up to n=100 can be prepared with fidelity >0.99 and success probability >0.95 under realistic noise parameters.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical path to scalable, high-fidelity generation of large Fock states, advancing bosonic quantum computing and metrology.

title: Quantum Circuit Overhead
authors: Oskar Słowik, Piotr Dulian, And Adam Sawicki
abstract:
Author(s): Oskar Słowik, Piotr Dulian, and Adam Sawicki

We introduce a measure for evaluating the efficiency of finite universal quantum gate sets [MATH], called the quantum circuit overhead (QCO), and the related notion of [MATH]-quantum circuit overhead [MATH]. QCO compares the circuit length required by [MATH] with the be…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012454] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a measure called quantum circuit overhead (QCO) to evaluate the efficiency of finite universal quantum gate sets.
motivation: To compare the circuit length required by different universal gate sets, which is important for optimizing quantum circuits.
method: Defines QCO as the ratio of circuit lengths needed to approximate any unitary using a given gate set versus an optimal set, and analyzes its properties.
result: Provides bounds and examples of QCO for common gate sets, showing how it quantifies overhead.
conclusion: QCO is a useful metric for assessing gate set efficiency, aiding in the design of quantum circuits.

title: Engineering The non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Skin Effects In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

We propose and systematically analyze a practical scheme for implementing a one-dimensional non-Hermitian (NH) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model using individually addressable Rydberg atom arrays. Our setup consists of an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, in which a synthetic gauge field is generate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012621] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to realize a non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with skin effects using Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topological phases, such as the skin effect, are of fundamental interest but challenging to realize experimentally. Rydberg atom arrays offer a controllable platform to engineer such Hamiltonians.
method: The scheme uses an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, synthetic gauge fields via Rydberg interactions, and dissipation to create non-Hermiticity. The system is analyzed through exact diagonalization and mean-field theory.
result: The model exhibits non-Hermitian skin effects and topological edge states, with parameters tunable via laser fields and atomic spacing.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays provide a viable platform for studying non-Hermitian topological physics, bridging quantum optics and condensed matter.

title: Estimating The Performance Boundary Of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes And Number-phase Codes
authors: Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Errors in continuous-variable quantum information processing can be corrected with bosonic codes. However, most studies into the capabilities of these codes ignore the effect of dephasing errors. Here, the authors benchmark different bosonic codes under general loss-dephasing noise and provide guidance for when each code is optimal in experimental scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012450] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks bosonic codes (GKP and number-phase codes) under general loss-dephasing noise, providing guidance for optimal code selection in experimental scenarios.
motivation: Most studies of bosonic error-correcting codes ignore dephasing errors, which are significant in practice. This work aims to characterize the performance boundary of GKP and number-phase codes under realistic noise.
method: The authors analyze the performance of GKP and number-phase codes under combined loss and dephasing noise, deriving thresholds and comparing their error-correction capabilities.
result: They identify regimes where each code outperforms the other, providing a performance boundary that depends on the relative strengths of loss and dephasing.
conclusion: The results offer practical guidance for choosing the optimal bosonic code in experimental continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Optimal Majoranas In Mesoscopic Kitaev Chains
authors: M. Alvarado, R. Seoane Souto, Maria José Calderón, And Ramón Aguado
abstract:
Author(s): M. Alvarado, R. Seoane Souto, Maria José Calderón, and Ramón Aguado

Kitaev chains realized in quantum dots coupled via superconducting segments provide a controllable platform for engineering Majorana zero modes (MZMs). In these systems, subgap states in the hybrid region mediate the effective coupling between quantum dots and determine the emergence of sweet spots …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034512] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies optimal sweet spots for Majorana zero modes in mesoscopic Kitaev chains realized with quantum dots and superconducting segments.
motivation: Majorana zero modes are promising for topological quantum computing, but their realization in hybrid systems requires precise control of subgap states.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a quantum-dot-based Kitaev chain, modeling subgap states and their effect on the effective coupling between dots to find parameter regimes that maximize MZM localization and robustness.
result: They identify optimal sweet spots where MZMs are well-localized and protected from quasiparticle poisoning, with clear signatures in the conductance spectrum.
conclusion: The results provide practical guidelines for engineering robust Majorana zero modes in mesoscopic hybrid devices, advancing the platform for topological qubits.

title: Theory Of Single-molecule Nmr Detected By Real-time Esr
authors: Baruch Horovitz And Alexander Shnirman
abstract:
Author(s): Baruch Horovitz and Alexander Shnirman

In relation to recent experimental data [Y. Manassen et al.,
tldr: A theoretical framework for detecting single-molecule NMR via real-time ESR, relevant to hybrid quantum sensing.
motivation: Recent experiments observed NMR oscillations in real-time ESR data, but a theoretical understanding was lacking.
method: Develops a theory of single-spin detection using ESR, modeling the coupled electron-nuclear spin system and the measurement backaction.
result: Shows that sharp NMR oscillations can be detected in real-time ESR under realistic conditions, with analysis of sensitivity and noise.
conclusion: The framework confirms feasibility and provides guidelines for experimental implementation of single-molecule NMR detection.

title: Triplet-assisted Leakage During Singlet-triplet Qubit Readout With A Quantum Point Contact
authors: Karol Kawa
abstract:
Author(s): Karol Kawa

Quantum point contact readout theory for singlet-triplet qubits in a lateral double quantum dot is extended by including tunneling of triplet configurations in a higher-energy level of the neighboring dot. This additional channel creates energetically allowed leakage pathways that modify the branch-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055302] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the theory of singlet-triplet qubit readout using a quantum point contact by including triplet-assisted leakage from higher-energy levels.
motivation: Accurate readout of singlet-triplet qubits is crucial for quantum computing; leakage due to higher-energy triplet states can reduce readout fidelity and must be understood.
method: The authors model the double quantum dot system with a quantum point contact, incorporating tunneling of triplet configurations into a higher-energy level of the neighboring dot, and compute the resulting leakage currents.
result: The additional triplet-assisted leakage pathways modify the branch-… (abstract truncated) and affect the readout signal.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating triplet-assisted leakage is important for improving singlet-triplet qubit readout fidelity in quantum dot systems.

title: 200 keV Energy Electron Irradiation Of Single-crystal Diamond: Quantification Of Vacancy And Nitrogen-vacancy Production
authors: Chloe C. Newsom, Ben L. Green, Mark E. Newton, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, And Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich
abstract:
Author(s): Chloe C. Newsom, Ben L. Green, Mark E. Newton, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, and Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich

Electron irradiation and annealing treatments are a method of color center/defect creation in diamond. The depth profile of defects created by low-energy 200 keV electrons in single-crystal high-purity (type II) electronic grade diamond grown via chemical vapor deposition has been investigated. The …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065203] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies vacancy and NV center production in diamond via 200 keV electron irradiation, providing depth profiles and conversion efficiencies.
motivation: Understanding defect creation in diamond is crucial for optimizing NV center formation, which is a key platform for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.
method: The authors use electron irradiation at 200 keV on single-crystal diamond, followed by annealing, and characterize defects using optical and electron paramagnetic resonance techniques.
result: They quantify the depth-dependent vacancy concentration and NV center yield, showing that low-energy electrons can efficiently create NV centers near the surface.
conclusion: Low-energy electron irradiation is a viable method for controlled NV center creation, with implications for diamond-based quantum technologies.

title: Convection Patterns In Nonequilibrium Kawasaki Dynamics At Low Temperature
authors: Meander van Den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, And François Huveneers
abstract:
Author(s): Meander Van den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, and François Huveneers

We study a conservative stochastic lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) coupled in the bulk to a heat bath, which leads to standard phase separation at low uniform temperatures. Instead, a macroscopic temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state. In this state, the usual long…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014147] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A study of convection patterns in a nonequilibrium steady state of a conservative stochastic lattice gas under a temperature gradient.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic temperature gradients drive phase separation and pattern formation in nonequilibrium systems.
method: Analyzes Kawasaki dynamics (conservative stochastic lattice gas) coupled to a heat bath, using theoretical and numerical methods to study steady-state behavior.
result: Identifies convection patterns and characterizes the nonequilibrium steady state, showing how the temperature gradient modifies the usual phase separation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium pattern formation in lattice gases, relevant to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics of driven systems.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in information spreading is observed in a classical many-body cellular automaton.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and information thermodynamics.
method: The study uses a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a 2D square lattice and analyzes information spreading via mutual information and other measures.
result: A clear dynamical phase transition is identified, characterized by a change in the growth of mutual information from logarithmic to linear in time.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that classical deterministic many-body systems can exhibit a phase transition in information spreading, analogous to quantum many-body localization-delocalization transitions.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States
authors: Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, And Montserrat Guilleumas
abstract:
Author(s): Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, and Montserrat Guilleumas

Quantum state control is a fundamental tool for quantum technologies. In this work, we propose and analyze the use of quantum optimal control to exploit the dipolar interaction of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, focusing on the generation of selected states with entangled circulation. This scheme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033121] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum optimal control to generate entangled current states in ultracold atoms on a lattice ring via dipolar interactions.
motivation: Controlling quantum states is essential for quantum technologies; here the goal is to exploit dipolar interactions to create entangled circulation states.
method: The authors apply quantum optimal control techniques to a system of ultracold atoms with dipolar interactions on a lattice ring.
result: They demonstrate the generation of selected entangled current states with high fidelity.
conclusion: The work shows that dipolar interactions can be harnessed for state control, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations through measurement-based rewards.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm uses a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements to iteratively build a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, demonstrating efficiency and scalability.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a practical tool for exploring fixed points and eigenstates of quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Spectroscopy Of Rydberg Levels Dressed By Linearly Polarized Rf Fields: Complementary Angular Response For Two Types Of Transition Ladders
authors: Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, And Niels Kjærgaard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, and Niels Kjærgaard

Rydberg atoms efficiently link photons between the radio-frequency (rf) and optical domains. They furnish a medium in which the presence of an rf field imprints on the transmission of a probe laser beam by altering the coherent coupling between atomic quantum states. The immutable atomic energy stru…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033089] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in Rydberg atoms dressed by a linearly polarized RF field, revealing complementary angular responses for two types of transition ladders.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum transduction between RF and optical domains, but the angular dependence of EIT spectra under linearly polarized RF fields is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform EIT spectroscopy on Rydberg atoms in a vapor cell, applying a linearly polarized RF field and measuring probe transmission as a function of RF polarization angle for two different excitation ladders (e.g., 5S-5P-5D and 5S-5P-5S).
result: They observe complementary angular responses: one ladder shows maximum EIT contrast when the RF polarization is parallel to the probe polarization, while the other shows maximum contrast when perpendicular.
conclusion: The complementary angular behavior can be exploited for polarization-sensitive RF sensing or to enhance the performance of Rydberg-based quantum transducers.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission using a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To realize nonreciprocal multiphoton sources for quantum networks and information processing.
method: A rotating two-mode cavity is directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling leapfrog multiphoton processes.
result: Nonreciprocal emission of multiphoton bundles is achieved, with direction-dependent properties.
conclusion: The spinning resonator platform offers a new way to generate nonreciprocal multiphoton states, useful for quantum communication.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms, including their small mass and long-range interactions, and propose experimental implementations using optical tweezers and Rydberg states.
result: Helium-3 atoms offer benefits such as faster gate operations and tunable hopping for quantum simulation, potentially enabling new regimes in quantum computing and simulation.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms present a promising platform for quantum science, with unique advantages over other atomic species for specific applications.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding extends Rydberg lifetimes in atom arrays, reducing relaxation errors for higher-fidelity two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but their two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by short Rydberg lifetimes due to blackbody radiation.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic environment to suppress blackbody radiation and measure Rydberg state lifetimes.
result: Rydberg lifetimes are significantly extended at cryogenic temperatures, leading to reduced relaxation errors and improved gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is an effective strategy to enhance coherence in neutral-atom quantum computers, bringing them closer to fault-tolerant thresholds.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics with high configurability using photonic hardware.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator.
result: Demonstrates a highly configurable and efficient simulation algorithm for a large class of quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical platform for studying quantum field theories.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications; spin-dependent squeezed states offer a path to surpass standard quantum limits.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a trapped-ion platform where spin-dependent squeezing is generated via a spin-motion coupling, and then used for displacement sensing.
result: They show that the proposed scheme achieves optimal sensitivity for displacement estimation, scaling with the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit coherence and understanding decoherence mechanisms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networking applications.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, including operator growth.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate beyond training data.
method: Fourier neural operators are applied to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in Floquet systems, leveraging spectral methods for efficient learning.
result: The method accurately predicts observable dynamics and operator growth for times beyond the training window, demonstrating generalization in frequency space.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A Colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are central to quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance for choosing appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis will help researchers navigate the diverse landscape of non-Markovian simulation methods and advance the field of open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates and reduce resource overhead. This review surveys the potential roles of qudits in quantum information processing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can simplify certain quantum circuits, reduce gate counts, and enable more efficient use of physical resources, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering advantages in gate decomposition and algorithm implementation, though challenges remain in control and error correction.

title: Probing Stringy Horizons With Pole Skipping In Nonmaximal Chaotic Systems
authors: Ping Gao And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Gao and Hong Liu

In this Letter, we study pole skipping in nonmaximally quantum chaotic systems. Using Rindler conformal field theories and the large-[MATH] Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev chain as illustrative examples, we argue that the pole skipping points of few-body operators organize into trajectories in the complex frequency-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pole skipping in nonmaximally chaotic systems, using Rindler CFTs and the SYK chain as examples, and argues that pole skipping points organize into trajectories in the complex frequency-momentum plane.
motivation: Pole skipping is a phenomenon in quantum chaos that reveals information about the underlying theory's horizon structure. The authors aim to extend the study to nonmaximally chaotic systems, which are more realistic and less understood.
method: The authors analyze pole skipping in Rindler conformal field theories and the large-q Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev chain, using analytic and numerical techniques to compute energy density correlators and identify pole skipping points.
result: They find that pole skipping points for few-body operators form trajectories in the complex frequency-momentum plane, and these trajectories are related to the Lyapunov exponent and butterfly velocity, even in nonmaximal chaos.
conclusion: The results suggest that pole skipping is a robust feature of quantum chaos that can probe stringy horizons and provide insights into the nature of quantum gravity and black hole physics.

title: Full Schmidt Characterization Of Spatiotemporally Entangled States Produced From Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Rakesh Pradhan And Girish Kulkarni
abstract:
Author(s): Rakesh Pradhan and Girish Kulkarni

The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been carried out until now due to the immense computational complexity arising from the large dimensionalities of the states. In this article, we utilize the rotat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013722] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper achieves the full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC using a rotation of the basis, enabling characterization of high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: Spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC have high dimensionality, making full Schmidt decomposition computationally challenging; previous work only provided partial characterizations.
method: The authors apply a rotation of the basis to simplify the Schmidt decomposition, reducing the computational complexity and enabling the full decomposition for the first time.
result: They obtain the full Schmidt decomposition, revealing the entanglement structure and quantifying the effective dimensionality of the spatiotemporal entanglement.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of spatiotemporal entanglement in SPDC, which is important for quantum information applications like quantum communication and computing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Delocalized Interacting Particles
authors: M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, And G. M. A. Almeida
abstract:
Author(s): M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, and G. M. A. Almeida

Quantum entanglement in systems of identical particles is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework used to define entanglement. To study the role of exchange statistics, we propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012452] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in a system of two distinguishable particles with exchange symmetry, revealing that delocalization and interaction can enhance entanglement.
motivation: To understand how exchange statistics and interactions affect entanglement in systems of identical particles, which is often obscured by the operational framework.
method: The authors propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchange interaction is introduced, and analyze the entanglement dynamics using concurrence.
result: They find that delocalization and interaction can lead to enhanced entanglement, and that the exchange interaction can be used to control entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange statistics in entanglement and offers a method to generate and control entanglement in identical particle systems.

title: Quantum Cryptography Compatible With Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices Based On Parrondo Dynamics In Discrete-time Quantum Walks
authors: Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, And Colin Benjamin
abstract:
Author(s): Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, and Colin Benjamin

Compatibility with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices is crucial for the realistic implementation of quantum cryptographic protocols. We investigate a cryptographic scheme based on discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs that exploits Parrondo dynamics, wherein periodic evolution e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012615] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A quantum cryptographic protocol using discrete-time quantum walks and Parrondo dynamics, designed for NISQ devices.
motivation: To develop quantum cryptography compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, addressing practical implementation challenges.
