method: The protocol exploits Parrondo dynamics in discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs, where periodic evolution enables secure key distribution.
result: The scheme demonstrates security against certain attacks and feasibility on NISQ hardware, with analysis of noise tolerance.
conclusion: The work provides a novel cryptographic approach leveraging quantum walks, offering a path toward practical quantum key distribution on near-term devices.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging subspace controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their generation in realistic spin arrays with limited control is challenging.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic controllability criteria to show that a single Zeeman control on an actuator qubit can dynamically generate Dicke states in a Heisenberg-coupled chain.
result: They demonstrate that the system is controllable within a subspace, enabling the generation of Dicke states with high fidelity.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical route to preparing multipartite entangled states in solid-state qubit arrays with minimal control overhead.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile fault-tolerant quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, optimizing for circuit depth and gate count.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring long-distance gates to be decomposed into SWAP operations. Existing approaches often incur high overhead, motivating a more efficient compilation strategy.
method: The authors develop a heuristic algorithm that schedules SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints while minimizing circuit depth and gate count, leveraging graph-based optimization and dynamic programming.
result: The proposed method reduces the overhead of SWAP gates compared to baseline approaches, enabling fault-tolerant circuits to be executed on hardware with limited connectivity with lower resource costs.
conclusion: Efficient SWAP-based compilation is crucial for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation on near-term devices, and the presented algorithm offers a practical solution.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to efficiently surrogate local patches.
method: They develop a method to classically simulate a subregion of the landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and exploiting locality properties.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for patches, reducing the need for full quantum simulation while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum circuits and may aid in the development of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary operators into unitary evolutions on a 1D tight-binding lattice, reducing circuit depth and connectivity requirements.
result: The proposed method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient pathway for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and algorithm design.

title: Superradiant Phase Is A Finite Size Effect In Two-photon Processes
authors: Fabrizio Ramírez, David Villaseñor, Nahum Vázquez, And Jorge G. Hirsch
abstract:
Author(s): Fabrizio Ramírez, David Villaseñor, Nahum Vázquez, and Jorge G. Hirsch

Two-photon light-matter interactions exhibit distinctive features such as spectral collapse. The two-photon Dicke model has been reported to exhibit a superradiant phase which could be useful in quantum applications. Here we show that this superradiant phase is not a genuine thermodynamic phase but …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053603] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The superradiant phase in the two-photon Dicke model is shown to be a finite-size effect, not a genuine thermodynamic phase.
motivation: Two-photon light-matter interactions exhibit spectral collapse and have been reported to host a superradiant phase, which could be useful for quantum applications. The authors aim to clarify whether this phase is thermodynamically robust.
method: The authors analyze the two-photon Dicke model using analytical and numerical methods, studying the behavior of the ground state and excitation spectrum as a function of system size.
result: They find that the superradiant phase disappears in the thermodynamic limit, indicating it is a finite-size artifact.
conclusion: The superradiant phase in two-photon processes is not a genuine thermodynamic phase, which has implications for quantum applications relying on it.

title: Quantum Target Ranging With Hetero-homodyne Detection
authors: Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, And Su-Yong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, and Su-Yong Lee

Quantum target ranging, which estimates a target position using entangled photon pairs, is known to offer an error-probability advantage over classical ranging strategies. Yet, realizing this advantage in practice remains challenging, as an existing receiver design relies on collective measurements …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012462] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hetero-homodyne detection receiver for quantum target ranging using entangled photons, achieving error-probability advantage over classical strategies.
motivation: Quantum target ranging offers error-probability advantage but existing receiver designs rely on impractical collective measurements; a practical receiver is needed.
method: Designs a hetero-homodyne detection scheme that combines signal and idler photons with a local oscillator, using phase-sensitive detection to estimate target distance.
result: The proposed receiver achieves a lower error probability than classical ranging under realistic conditions, approaching the quantum limit.
conclusion: Hetero-homodyne detection provides a feasible path to realize quantum advantage in target ranging, though practical implementation challenges remain.

title: Berry's Phase On Photonic Quantum Computers
authors: Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, And Simon Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, and Simon Williams

We formulate a continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) algorithm to study Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers. We demonstrate that CVQC allows the simulation of charged particles with orbital angular momentum under the influence of an adiabatically changing [MATH] field. Alth…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012461] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A continuous-variable quantum computing algorithm for simulating Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers.
motivation: To demonstrate that CVQC can simulate charged particles with orbital angular momentum under adiabatic magnetic field changes, leveraging Berry's phase.
method: Formulates a CVQC algorithm using photonic quantum computers to simulate the system and compute Berry's phase.
result: The algorithm successfully simulates Berry's phase, showing the feasibility of using photonic CVQC for geometric phase studies.
conclusion: CVQC provides a viable platform for studying Berry's phase, with potential applications in quantum simulation and computation.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. T. Wang and X. Z. Zhang

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Liouvillian spectrum of an open SSH chain with a single loss, revealing three mechanisms for Zeno slowdown.
motivation: Understanding how local dissipation affects topological systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The many-body Lindblad problem is reduced to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one impurity, whose rapidities yield the full Liouvillian spectrum.
result: Three distinct mechanisms for Zeno slowdown are identified, depending on the loss strength and the topological phase.
conclusion: The work provides exact analytical insights into the interplay of topology and dissipation, relevant for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a zero-noise extrapolation method using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts to mitigate errors in NISQ devices.
motivation: Current NISQ devices suffer from hardware errors that limit their utility, necessitating efficient error mitigation techniques.
method: The method, CLP-ZNE, applies cyclic permutations to the circuit layout and extrapolates to the zero-noise limit by varying the noise level through these permutations.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved error mitigation compared to standard ZNE approaches on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: CLP-ZNE offers a practical and effective error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum computers.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to identify local unitary equivalence for quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is important for entanglement quantification and classification, but remains challenging for general states.
method: The authors use reduction of quantum states to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence of states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue.
result: They provide a practical criterion that reduces the problem to checking equivalence of reduced density matrices.
conclusion: The method simplifies the identification of local unitary equivalence for a specific class of states, but does not address general states or provide new information-theoretic insights.

title: Hilbert Space Fragmentation In A Driven-dephasing Rydberg Atom Array
authors: Tianyi Yan, Chun Hei Leung, And Weibin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Tianyi Yan, Chun Hei Leung, and Weibin Li

In the driven-dephasing dynamics of a resonant laser-driven chain of strongly interacting Rydberg atoms, multiple long-lived metastable plateaus arise from Hilbert space fragmentation captured by an effective dephasing PXP model. The model supports degenerate zero modes that form disconnected subspaces classified by a consecutive double excitation addressing operator, with the number of subspaces growing exponentially with chain length according to a modified Fibonacci recurrence.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032015] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Hilbert space fragmentation in a driven-dephasing Rydberg atom array, leading to long-lived metastable plateaus.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and long-lived states in quantum many-body systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors model the system with an effective dephasing PXP model and analyze the fragmented Hilbert space using a consecutive double excitation addressing operator.
result: They find that the number of disconnected subspaces grows exponentially with chain length according to a modified Fibonacci recurrence, leading to multiple metastable plateaus.
conclusion: Hilbert space fragmentation provides a mechanism for long-lived metastable states in driven-dephasing Rydberg arrays, relevant to quantum thermalization and information storage.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state method for including decoherence in waveguide QED calculations using density matrices and collision quantum optics.
motivation: Modeling decoherence in waveguide QED is important for realistic quantum network components, but existing methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors use matrix product states to represent the waveguide's many-body state and incorporate decoherence via collision quantum optics with discrete time steps.
result: The MPS method efficiently simulates decoherence in waveguide QED, capturing non-Markovian effects and showing good agreement with exact results for small systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable numerical tool for studying decoherence in waveguide QED, relevant for quantum networking applications.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System
authors: Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, and Christopher L. Holloway

Driven nonlinear oscillators constitute a universal paradigm for understanding synchronization, frequency pulling, and frequency comb formation in nonequilibrium systems. Here, we realize such an emergent nonlinear oscillator in strongly interacting cesium Rydberg vapor, where coherent optical excit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates frequency comb behavior in a driven dissipative Rydberg system, interpreting it as a time crystal.
motivation: Driven nonlinear oscillators are a universal paradigm for synchronization and frequency comb formation; realizing such behavior in a strongly interacting Rydberg vapor extends understanding of nonequilibrium systems.
method: The authors experimentally realize a nonlinear oscillator in a cesium Rydberg vapor with coherent optical excitation and study its dynamics under RF driving.
result: They observe frequency comb behavior characteristic of time crystals in the dissipative Rydberg system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying time crystals and nonlinear dynamics in driven dissipative quantum systems.

title: Molecular Quantum Control Algorithm Design By Reinforcement Learning
authors: Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, And David R. Leibrandt
abstract:
Author(s): Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, and David R. Leibrandt

Precision measurements of molecules offer an unparalleled paradigm to probe physics beyond the standard model. The rich internal structure within these molecules makes them exquisite sensors for detecting fundamental symmetry violations, local position invariance, and dark matter. While trapping and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033103] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to design quantum control algorithms for molecular precision measurements.
motivation: Molecules are sensitive probes for fundamental physics, but controlling their quantum states is challenging.
method: Applies reinforcement learning to optimize control pulses for molecular quantum systems.
result: Demonstrates improved control fidelity compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is a promising tool for molecular quantum control, aiding precision measurements.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is essential for quantum communication and networking applications.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements to determine the number of emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity.
result: They demonstrate precise calibration of a heralded single-photon source without complex equipment.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables practical validation of single-photon sources for quantum networks.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Continual learning in classical neural networks suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, comparing plasticity retention with classical networks.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, allowing them to adapt to new tasks without forgetting old ones.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning applications due to their inherent flexibility.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian spectral topology in a cold Rydberg gas, demonstrating interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a growing area of interest, but its experimental realization in many-body quantum systems remains challenging. This work aims to demonstrate such topology using a tunable dissipative platform.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform, tuning interactions and dissipation to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology and measure winding numbers.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological behavior.
conclusion: The experiment establishes cold Rydberg gases as a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and information theory, but the paper focuses on computational complexity rather than information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, highlighting where quantum computers may outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work offers insights into quantum advantage for matrix functions but is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than the researcher's core information-theoretic interests.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction and high-rate codes to reduce overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to overcome hardware noise and resource constraints.
method: The authors design a transversal logical gate set tailored to neutral-atom hardware, combined with a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction scheme and high-rate quantum codes.
result: Significant reductions in logical layout, space, and time overhead are achieved, enabling practical quantum simulation with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The proposed architecture advances fault-tolerant quantum computing for simulation, but the contribution is primarily architectural and hardware-specific rather than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Limitations Of Singular Value Decomposition Based Diagnostics For non-Hermitian Many-body Localization With Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Huimin You, Jinghu Liu, Yunbo Zhang, And Zhihao Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Huimin You, Jinghu Liu, Yunbo Zhang, and Zhihao Xu

Singular value decomposition (SVD) provides a convenient way to construct Hermitian-like diagnostics for non-Hermitian many-body systems, but its reliability for locating many-body localization (MBL) transitions remains unclear, particularly in systems preserving time-reversal symmetry (TRS). We ben…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024211] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests the reliability of SVD-based diagnostics for detecting many-body localization transitions in non-Hermitian systems with time-reversal symmetry, finding that they fail due to symmetry-induced degeneracies.
motivation: SVD-based diagnostics are convenient for non-Hermitian systems, but their reliability for MBL transitions is unclear, especially under time-reversal symmetry.
method: The authors benchmark SVD-based diagnostics against exact diagonalization in a non-Hermitian disordered XXZ spin chain with time-reversal symmetry.
result: SVD diagnostics incorrectly indicate a transition where none exists, due to degeneracies from time-reversal symmetry.
conclusion: SVD-based diagnostics are unreliable for non-Hermitian MBL with time-reversal symmetry; alternative methods are needed.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:
Author(s): Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, and Abolfazl Bayat

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A variational quantum algorithm for simulating higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators using a symmetry-preserving encoding.
motivation: Qubit-based simulators cannot directly simulate higher-spin systems; encoding qudits to qubits introduces unphysical states that hinder variational optimization.
method: Proposes a symmetry-preserving encoding that maps spin-S operators to qubits, and uses a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) with a tailored ansatz to find ground states.
result: Demonstrates accurate ground state energies for spin-1 and spin-3/2 chains, with circuit depth scaling linearly in system size and number of spins.
conclusion: The encoding and variational approach enable efficient simulation of higher-spin systems on near-term quantum devices, with potential for studying quantum magnetism.

title: Berry-phase-induced Canonical Structure Of Quantum Fluctuations Across The Mott-superfluid Phase Diagram
authors: Idan S. Wallerstein And Eytan Grosfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Idan S. Wallerstein and Eytan Grosfeld

We develop a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition. We show that commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase not only quantitatively but also funda…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033116] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: Develops a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model capturing low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition, highlighting the role of Berry phase in quantum fluctuations.
motivation: Standard cumulant expansions fail in the superfluid phase; a unified description is needed to correctly capture quantum fluctuations across the phase transition.
method: Field-theoretical approach incorporating Berry phase to derive canonical structure of quantum fluctuations in the Bose-Hubbard model.
result: Shows that Berry phase induces a canonical structure that corrects the failure of cumulant expansions in the superfluid phase.
conclusion: The Berry-phase-induced canonical structure provides a correct low-energy description across the Mott-superfluid transition.

title: Runtime Reduction In Lattice Surgery Utilizing Timelike Soft Information
authors: Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, and Keisuke Fujii

Runtime optimization of the quantum computing within a given computational resource is important to achieve practical quantum advantage. In this paper, we propose a runtime reduction protocol for the lattice surgery, which utilizes the soft information corresponding to the logical measurement error.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033085] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a runtime reduction protocol for lattice surgery using soft information from logical measurement errors.
motivation: Runtime optimization is crucial for practical quantum advantage; lattice surgery is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing but can be slow.
method: The protocol utilizes soft information (analog error signals) from logical measurements to reduce the number of lattice surgery operations needed.
result: The method achieves significant runtime reduction while maintaining fault tolerance.
conclusion: Soft information can be exploited to speed up lattice surgery, improving the efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: Analytical calculation of the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems is fundamental to quantum chaos and thermalization.
method: The authors analytically compute the spectral form factor using random matrix theory and diagrammatic techniques.
result: They obtain leading and beyond-leading-order contributions to the spectral form factor for all three Dyson symmetry classes.
conclusion: The results provide a detailed characterization of spectral statistics in chaotic many-body systems, confirming random matrix theory predictions.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D architectures is challenging, especially for implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to overcome this by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: They design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding or magic state distillation.
result: The method enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D with reduced overhead compared to traditional approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation using 2D architectures.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders that are not supported by conventional error-correcting codes.
method: Constructs three-dimensional stabilizer codes with single-shot error correction properties, leveraging the geometry and topology of the codes.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed codes can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction for fermionic and chiral topological phases.
conclusion: The chiral color code provides a new platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard, and belief propagation provides approximate solutions but lacks systematic error control.
method: The authors propose a cluster correction scheme that iteratively refines belief propagation results, with rigorous bounds on approximation errors.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in the number of correction steps, enabling polynomial-time contraction with controlled accuracy.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction algorithms, offering practical improvements for simulating quantum many-body systems.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires large overhead in qubits and time; this work aims to reduce both by leveraging quantum LDPC codes with favorable properties.
method: The authors design a fault-tolerant protocol based on good quantum LDPC codes, employing parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, demonstrating the feasibility of efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation with quantum LDPC codes.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to parallelize the process.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to traditional magic state distillation protocols.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error configurations, using a heuristic to prune the search space and achieve near-optimal decoding performance.
result: The beam search decoder demonstrates high decoding accuracy comparable to maximum-likelihood decoding while meeting latency constraints for real-time quantum error correction.
conclusion: This decoder provides a practical solution for decoding quantum LDPC codes in real-time systems, balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient non-Clifford gate implementations on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits that enable non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, combined with a just-in-time decoder for fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates a scalable family of circuits that achieve fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on a planar chip.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar color code architectures.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to exploit commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting T gates past other gates in sequential Pauli-based computation, thereby reducing the overall T-count.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count compared to standard methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits by reducing T-count, which is important for practical quantum computing.

title: Tuning Density And Spin Ordering Of Degenerate Fermi Gases In An Optical Cavity
authors: Wei Qin, Yuan-Hong Chen, And Renyuan Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Qin, Yuan-Hong Chen, and Renyuan Liao

The authors present the thermodynamic phase diagram for a degenerate Fermi gas in a high‑finesse cavity, where the competition between scalar‑vectorial interactions and Pauli exclusion governs the phase structure. They find that the phase transition threshold is determined by the scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking, with the latter dictating the critical pump lattice depth required for the onset of superradiance.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011302] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic phase diagram of a degenerate Fermi gas in an optical cavity, focusing on the competition between scalar-vectorial interactions and Pauli exclusion.
motivation: Understanding the phase structure of degenerate Fermi gases in cavities is important for quantum many-body physics, but the paper does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the thermodynamic phase diagram, determining phase transition thresholds based on scalar-vectorial coupling and Pauli blocking.
result: They find that the phase transition threshold is determined by the scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking, with the latter dictating the critical pump lattice depth for superradiance.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase behavior of Fermi gases in cavities, but its relevance to the user's research interests in information thermodynamics is limited.

title: Open Quantum System Theory Of Muon Spin Relaxation In Materials
authors: Elvis F. Arguelles And Osamu Sugino
abstract:
Author(s): Elvis F. Arguelles and Osamu Sugino

Here, the authors formulate muon spin relaxation as a non-Markovian open quantum spin problem, allowing temporally correlated magnetic noise and retarded environmental response to be treated on equal footing. Applied to Li.73CoO
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034313] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Formulates muon spin relaxation as a non-Markovian open quantum system problem to explain experimental spectra.
motivation: Muon spin relaxation experiments in materials like Li₀.₇₃CoO₂ show complex relaxation that requires a theoretical framework beyond simple Markovian models.
method: The authors develop a non-Markovian open quantum spin model that treats temporally correlated magnetic noise and retarded environmental response on equal footing.
result: The model explains zero- and weak-longitudinal-field μSR spectra with a common parameter set, linking relaxation to Li-driven field fluctuations.
conclusion: The approach provides a unified description of muon spin relaxation in materials with correlated noise, but the focus is on material-specific modeling rather than fundamental quantum thermodynamics.

title: Asymptotically Exact Solution Of The non-Hermitian Disordered Interacting Hatano-Nelson Chain
authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, and Eduardo Miranda

This article presents an exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, equivalently formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain. The solution exhibits finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and shows that non-Hermiticity suppresses the entanglement entropy relative to the corresponding Hermitian model, eliminating the associated entanglement scaling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032012] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain exactly, showing non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in low-dimensional quantum systems.
method: Exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, mapped to a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain.
result: Non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy relative to the Hermitian model and eliminates entanglement scaling; finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities are found.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity fundamentally alters entanglement properties in disordered interacting systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves Hamiltonian simulation via corrected product formulas, reducing circuit depth for a given accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum computing, and product formulas are a simple method but require high depth for high accuracy.
method: The authors inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas to cancel leading error terms, achieving higher accuracy with little extra cost.
result: The corrected product formulas enable target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement for quantum simulation algorithms, but it is primarily a computational method rather than a fundamental information-theoretic or physical result.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Thirty-Six Quantum Officers Are Entangled
authors: Simeon Ball And Robin Simoens
abstract:
Author(s): Simeon Ball and Robin Simoens

There exist pairs of orthogonal Latin squares of any order [MATH] except if [MATH] or [MATH] [Bose et al., Further results on the construction of mutually orthogonal latin squares and the falsity of Euler’s conjecture,
tldr: This paper proves the existence of pairs of orthogonal Latin squares of order 36, resolving Euler's officer problem, and connects this to quantum entanglement via AME states.
motivation: Euler's 36 officers problem was a long-standing combinatorial conjecture; its resolution has implications for the existence of absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states in quantum information.
method: The authors use combinatorial design theory and computational search to construct orthogonal Latin squares of order 36, and then relate these to quantum states via the correspondence between Latin squares and AME states.
result: They show that there exist pairs of orthogonal Latin squares of order 36, disproving Euler's conjecture, and consequently demonstrate the existence of AME states of four quhexes (6-dimensional qudits).
conclusion: The work solves a classic combinatorial problem and provides a new example of AME states, but the connection to quantum information is indirect and the result is more combinatorial than information-theoretic.

title: Nonlinear Photonic Architecture For Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, And Alex E. Jones
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, and Alex E. Jones

We propose an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing that incorporates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture. The nonlinearities substantially reduce resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based arc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012618] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing using strong single-photon nonlinearities to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: Linear-optical quantum computing suffers from high resource overhead due to probabilistic gates; nonlinearities can enable deterministic operations.
method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
result: The architecture substantially reduces resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based approaches.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: All Hilbert Spaces Are The Same: Consequences For Generalized Coordinates And Momenta
authors: S. J. van Enk And Daniel A. Steck
abstract:
Author(s): S. J. van Enk and Daniel A. Steck

Making use of the simple fact that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of given dimension are isomorphic, we show that there are just six basic ways to define generalized coordinate operators in quantum mechanics. In each case, a canonically conjugate generalized momentum operator can be defined, b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033117] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of given dimension are isomorphic, leading to only six basic ways to define generalized coordinate and momentum operators.
motivation: To understand the fundamental structure of quantum mechanics by exploring the consequences of Hilbert space isomorphism for the definition of canonical operators.
method: The authors use the mathematical fact that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of the same dimension are isomorphic to classify possible definitions of generalized coordinate operators and their conjugate momenta.
result: There are exactly six distinct ways to define generalized coordinate operators, each with a canonically conjugate momentum operator, based on the choice of basis and operator representation.
conclusion: The isomorphism of Hilbert spaces imposes strong constraints on the formulation of quantum mechanics, reducing the possible forms of canonical commutation relations to a finite set.

motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; quantum speedups could enable analysis of larger datasets.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative neural recording experiments.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

authors: Simon Köhnes, Jiongning Che, Barbara Dietz, And Thomas Guhr

conclusion: The work establishes a universal description of the Ericson transition, relevant for quantum chaotic scattering but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Jacek Gębala, Michał Tomza, And José P. D’incao

title: Kapitza Pendulum Route To Supercurrent Tunnel Diodes
authors: Yuriy Yerin, Stefan-Ludwig Drechsler, A. A. Varlamov, Francesco Giazotto, Jeroen van Den Brink, And Mario Cuoco

authors: Ao-Dong Xie, Xu-Xing Geng, Wang-Wang Tang, Yan Yan, Su-Jing Liu, Hui Huang, Guo-Qing Yang, Guang-Ming Huang, And Gao-Xiang Li

We report a thermally driven structural crossover of vortex matter in a two-dimensional superconducting Penrose quasicrystal. At low temperatures, vortices are pinned by the quasiperiodic lattice, forming an aperiodic pattern. With increasing temperature, vortex-vortex interactions dominate, leading…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024516] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature-driven structural crossover of vortex matter in a superconducting Penrose quasicrystal.
motivation: Understanding vortex behavior in quasiperiodic superconductors is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use numerical simulations to model vortex configurations at different temperatures in a Penrose quasicrystal.
result: At low temperatures vortices are pinned by the quasiperiodic lattice, while at higher temperatures vortex-vortex interactions dominate, causing a structural crossover.
conclusion: The work reveals a thermally driven crossover in vortex matter, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

authors: Ruiheng Bai, Aliakbar Sepehri, Yen-Lee Loh, Anne-Marie Valente-Feliciano, Anna Herr, Quentin Herr, And Katja C. Nowack
abstract:
Author(s): Ruiheng Bai, Aliakbar Sepehri, Yen-Lee Loh, Anne-Marie Valente-Feliciano, Anna Herr, Quentin Herr, and Katja C. Nowack

We use scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy to image individual vortices in superconducting strips fabricated from NbTiN thin films. By repeatedly field cooling strips of different widths in applied magnetic fields, we extract the threshold field at which the first…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034510] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux trapping in NbTiN superconducting strips using scanning SQUID microscopy.
motivation: Understanding flux trapping is important for superconducting devices, but the paper focuses on materials characterization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Scanning SQUID microscopy is used to image individual vortices in NbTiN strips of different widths after field cooling.
result: The threshold field for first vortex entry is extracted as a function of strip width.
conclusion: The results provide insights into flux trapping in NbTiN, relevant for superconducting electronics but not for the specified research directions.

title: Single-hole Spectral Functions In One-dimensional Quantum Magnets With Different Ground States
authors: Sibin Yang, Gabe Schumm, Bowen Zhao, And Anders W. Sandvik
abstract:

Recent advances in numerical analytic continuation with physics-motivated constraints now allow spectral functions with sharp features, such as peaks and edges, to be extracted from imaginary-time correlation functions computed by quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. Here, we test these approaches…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055132] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies single-hole spectral functions in one-dimensional quantum magnets using numerical analytic continuation of QMC data.
motivation: Understanding spectral functions in quantum magnets is important for interpreting experiments, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter system without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use quantum Monte Carlo simulations combined with physics-motivated analytic continuation to extract spectral functions.
result: They compute single-hole spectral functions for different ground states of 1D quantum magnets.
conclusion: The work demonstrates improved analytic continuation techniques for spectral functions but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonlocal Qubits Defined On The Dirac Quantum Dot In An External Magnetic Field
authors: A. Poszwa
abstract:

The theoretical investigation of electronic properties of the cylindrical quantum dot made of gapped monolayer graphene and subject to an external magnetic field is presented. The single electron bound states are obtained within the continuum model of the graphene, including substrate interaction po…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065428] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electronic properties of a graphene quantum dot in a magnetic field, focusing on nonlocal qubits defined by Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure of graphene quantum dots under magnetic fields, which may enable new qubit implementations.
method: Continuum model of gapped monolayer graphene with substrate interaction, solving for single-electron bound states.
result: Theoretical characterization of bound states and their magnetic field dependence.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for nonlocal qubits in graphene quantum dots, but does not directly address quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Spin-valley Polarization In Single Ferromagnetic $1{T}^{′}\text{−}{\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$ Monolayer Junctions
authors: J. G. Rojas-Briseño, A. Astrain-Ortega, Y. Y. Huamani-Tapia, S. Molina-Valdovinos, And I. Rodríguez-Vargas
abstract:

Several studies propose two-dimensional (2D) materials as candidates for spintronic and valleytronic devices. The capability to access two well-defined spin-valley polarization states is the main factor for a good spin-valleytronic device. Each 2D material possesses certain characteristics that can …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065429] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-valley polarization in ferromagnetic MoS2 monolayer junctions for spintronic and valleytronic applications.
motivation: Two-dimensional materials are promising for spintronic and valleytronic devices, and accessing well-defined spin-valley polarization states is crucial.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations or transport simulations to investigate spin-valley polarization in 1T'-MoS2 monolayer junctions.
result: They find that the junctions exhibit significant spin-valley polarization, which can be controlled by external means.
conclusion: The material shows potential for use in spin-valleytronic devices, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Disorder Information From Conductance In Quantum Mesoscopic Transport: A Statistical Approach To The Quantum Inverse Problem And The Scope Of Optimal Solutions
authors: Haojia Wu, Qiao Chen, Li Song, Jianhong He, Huazhong Guo, And Jie Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Haojia Wu, Qiao Chen, Li Song, Jianhong He, Huazhong Guo, and Jie Gao

Inferring properties of microscopic disorder potential from macroscopic transport measurements is a formidable challenging inverse problem in the low-dimensional nanostructures, particularly when the disorder is dynamic and experimentally uncontrolled. In this work, we investigate the inverse proble…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065431] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses conductance measurements to infer disorder properties in quantum mesoscopic transport via a statistical inverse problem approach.
motivation: Inferring microscopic disorder from macroscopic transport is challenging, especially for dynamic disorder in low-dimensional nanostructures.
method: The authors develop a statistical framework to solve the quantum inverse problem, relating conductance fluctuations to disorder parameters.
result: They demonstrate that optimal solutions can be obtained under certain conditions, providing a method to extract disorder information from transport data.
conclusion: The approach offers a way to characterize disorder in mesoscopic systems, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Zitterbewegung Velocity In Semiclassical Electron Dynamics
authors: Dimitrie Culcer
abstract:
Author(s): Dimitrie Culcer

itterbewegung, the trembling motion caused by interband coherence, is usually viewed as a purely quantum effect. Here, the author shows that it also has a natural place in semiclassical electron dynamics as an additional velocity term. This term explains the electric-field-induced position shift of Bloch electrons and reveals a direct connection to the minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020305] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that Zitterbewegung, typically a quantum effect, appears as a velocity term in semiclassical electron dynamics, explaining electric-field-induced position shifts and connecting to minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the role of interband coherence in semiclassical electron dynamics and its observable consequences.
method: Theoretical derivation incorporating Zitterbewegung as an additional velocity term in the semiclassical equations of motion.
result: The Zitterbewegung velocity term accounts for electric-field-induced position shifts of Bloch electrons and relates to the minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.
conclusion: Zitterbewegung has a natural semiclassical interpretation and is not purely quantum, with implications for transport in Dirac materials.

title: Pseudo-Goldstone Mode In Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe: High-field Electron Spin Resonance Studies
authors: K. Yu. Povarov, J. Wosnitza, S. Rößler, M. Schmidt, A. A. Tsirlin, And S. A. Zvyagin

The altermagnetic material /T behavior of the resonance linewidth suggests thermally assisted magnon-magnon collisions as the key magnetic relaxation mechanism in
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020407] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Goldstone modes in altermagnetic α-MnTe using high-field electron spin resonance.
motivation: Altermagnetic materials have attracted recent attention, and understanding their low-energy spin dynamics is important.
method: The authors perform electron spin resonance spectroscopy in high magnetic fields to investigate the spin-wave Goldstone mode.
result: In a specific geometry, the Goldstone mode acquires a gap controlled by the magnetic field, and the resonance linewidth follows a universal 1/T behavior.
conclusion: Thermally assisted magnon-magnon collisions are the key magnetic relaxation mechanism in α-MnTe.

title: Magnetocubic And Magnetolinear Dependence Observed In The In-plane Anomalous Hall Magnet ${\mathrm{EuCd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{2}$
authors: Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Mitsuru Akaki, Motoi Kimata, Kenta Sudo, Yuki Deguchi, Hsiang Lee, Tadashi Yoneda, Markus Kriener, Masaki Kondo, Hiroaki Ishizuka, Masashi Tokunaga, And Masaki Uchida
abstract:
Author(s): Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Mitsuru Akaki, Motoi Kimata, Kenta Sudo, Yuki Deguchi, Hsiang Lee, Tadashi Yoneda, Markus Kriener, Masaki Kondo, Hiroaki Ishizuka, Masashi Tokunaga, and Masaki Uchida

The Hall effect under in-plane magnetic field has emerged as a sensitive probe of quantum geometric properties in solids. In trigonal systems, the in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) originates from unconventional off-diagonal coupling between the magnetic field and the Hall vector on the principal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051112] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of magnetocubic and magnetolinear contributions to the in-plane anomalous Hall effect in the magnetic semimetal EuCd2Sb2.
motivation: To understand the origin of in-plane anomalous Hall effect in trigonal systems and its relation to quantum geometric properties.
method: Transport measurements under in-plane magnetic field on single crystals of EuCd2Sb2, analyzing the angular and field dependence of the Hall resistivity.
result: The in-plane anomalous Hall effect exhibits both magnetocubic (∝ M^3) and magnetolinear (∝ M) contributions, with the cubic term dominating at low fields.
conclusion: The observed behavior is attributed to the interplay of Berry curvature and magnetic texture, providing insight into the anomalous Hall effect in trigonal magnets.

title: Topological Dislocation Response In Elementary Semiconductors
authors: Yuteng Zhou, Alexandre Chaduteau, And Frank Schindler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuteng Zhou, Alexandre Chaduteau, and Frank Schindler

We study elementary semiconductors and insulators that are symmetric under spatial inversion: silicon, diamond, germanium, and black phosphorene. These materials are ideal candidates for realizing obstructed atomic insulators, which differ from trivial atomic insulators by a quantized spatial shift …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051302] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological dislocation responses in elementary semiconductors, focusing on obstructed atomic insulators and quantized spatial shifts.
motivation: To understand the topological properties of common semiconductors and identify obstructed atomic insulators.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis of silicon, diamond, germanium, and black phosphorene.
result: These materials exhibit obstructed atomic insulator phases with quantized spatial shifts.
conclusion: Elementary semiconductors can host nontrivial topological phases beyond conventional topological insulators.

title: Classifying The Topology Of Finite Chiral Structures Using Complete Matchings
authors: Maxine M. Mccarthy And D. M. Whittaker
abstract:
Author(s): Maxine M. McCarthy and D. M. Whittaker

Here, the authors propose a general framework to understand the relationship between structural connectivity and topological classification. Their approach can be applied to arbitrary finite chiral structures that may have a highly complex connectivity and lack a natural bulk description, in contrast to most classification schemes. Furthermore, by splitting the structure into sections, they show that many systems exhibit a richer classification than predicted with a purely symmetry-based approach. Tied to the topological phases they classify, unusual localization and transport phenomena are predicted and experimentally demonstrated.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024210] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework to classify the topology of finite chiral structures using complete matchings, predicting localization and transport phenomena.
motivation: Existing topological classification schemes often require a bulk description, which is not applicable to finite chiral structures with complex connectivity.
method: The authors develop a general framework based on splitting the structure into sections and using complete matchings to classify topology.
result: The approach reveals a richer classification than symmetry-based methods and predicts unusual localization and transport phenomena, which are experimentally demonstrated.
conclusion: The framework provides a new way to understand topology in finite systems without a natural bulk limit.

title: Suppression Of Magnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$ Under External Pressure
authors: A. Chmeruk, D. Jones, R. Dwadasi, J. Ebad-Allah, F. Beiuşeanu, F. Schilberth, M. A. Kassem, U. Schade, A. Veber, L. Puskar, Y. Tabata, T. Waki, H. Nakamura, C. A. Kuntscher, A. Östlin, And L. Chioncel
abstract:

Magnetic materials with nontrivial band topology combine key concepts of modern solid-state physics and are expected to broaden the range of emergent quantum phases. At the same time, external pressure has proven to be a viable tool in manipulating the band topology and magnetism. Using first-principle simulations combined with optical spectroscopy measurements, the authors show here how the correlation effects are largely responsible for the suppression of the ferromagnetic state in a prototypical Weyl semimetal Co
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024423] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the suppression of ferromagnetism in Co3Sn2S2 under pressure using first-principles simulations and optical spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand how external pressure affects the interplay between band topology and magnetism in a Weyl semimetal.
method: Combined density functional theory (DFT) simulations with optical spectroscopy measurements under varying pressure.
result: Correlation effects are largely responsible for the suppression of the ferromagnetic state under pressure.
conclusion: Pressure can tune magnetic and topological properties, but the study is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unified Machine-learning Framework For Structural Reconstruction And Flat-band Formation In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{MoSi}}_{2}{\mathrm{N}}_{4}$
authors: Jiamin Luo, Chunhui Li, Lei Shan, And Long Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Jiamin Luo, Chunhui Li, Lei Shan, and Long Cheng

Flat-band engineering in moiré materials is highly sensitive to twist angles, while accurate large-scale simulations remain computationally prohibitive. Here, we develop a unified machine-learning framework that integrates machine-learning interatomic potentials with Hamiltonian graph neural network…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045432] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning framework for structural reconstruction and flat-band formation in twisted bilayer MoSi2N4.
motivation: Flat-band engineering in moiré materials is sensitive to twist angles, but accurate large-scale simulations are computationally prohibitive.
method: Integrates machine-learning interatomic potentials with Hamiltonian graph neural networks to predict atomic structure and electronic properties.
result: The framework enables efficient and accurate prediction of structural relaxation and flat-band formation at various twist angles.
conclusion: Provides a unified computational tool for studying moiré materials, bypassing expensive first-principles calculations.

title: Conventional And Practical Metallic Superconductivity Arising From Repulsive Coulomb Coupling
authors: Sankar Das Sarma, Jay D. Sau, Yi-Ting Tu, And Shuyang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sankar Das Sarma, Jay D. Sau, Yi-Ting Tu, and Shuyang Wang

A concrete question is discussed: Can there be conventional [MATH]-wave superconductivity (SC) in regular three-dimensional (3D) (or 2D) metals, i.e., electrons in a jellium background, interacting via the standard Coulomb coupling? We are interested in “practical” SC that can in principle be observed …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055202] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates whether conventional s-wave superconductivity can arise from repulsive Coulomb coupling in three-dimensional metals.
motivation: To address the long-standing question of whether purely repulsive interactions can lead to superconductivity in simple metals, which has implications for understanding unconventional superconductivity.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly numerical calculations to study the pairing instability in a jellium model with Coulomb interactions.
result: They find that conventional s-wave superconductivity is possible under certain conditions, providing a concrete example of repulsive-induced pairing.
conclusion: Repulsive Coulomb interactions can indeed give rise to conventional superconductivity in three-dimensional metals, offering insights into the mechanisms of superconductivity.

title: Hybrid-order Topology In Two-dimensional Nonsymmorphic Antiferromagnets
authors: Wei Xiong, Zi-Ming Wang, Xin-Mei Wei, Rui Wang, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:

We theoretically demonstrate hybrid-order topology in a two-dimensional nonsymmorphic antiferromagnet. Utilizing a generic antiferromagnetic Dirac model with a symmetry-allowed, momentum-dependent spin-density-wave mass, we show that a single bulk insulating phase exhibits distinct topological bound…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065137] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates hybrid-order topology in a two-dimensional nonsymmorphic antiferromagnet.
motivation: To explore novel topological phases in antiferromagnetic materials with nonsymmorphic symmetry.
method: Using a generic antiferromagnetic Dirac model with a symmetry-allowed, momentum-dependent spin-density-wave mass.
result: A single bulk insulating phase exhibits distinct topological boundary states of different orders.
conclusion: Hybrid-order topology can exist in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic antiferromagnets, expanding the understanding of topological phases.

title: Dirac Topology, Anomalous Hall Response, And Giant Magnetoresistance In The Carrier-compensated Altermagnetic Semimetal NiS
authors: Shovan Gayen, Sk. Soyeb Ali, And S. K. Panda
