We combine first-principles density-functional theory, Berry-curvature analysis, semiclassical Boltzmann transport, and atomistic spin dynamics to establish hexagonal NiS as a compensated [MATH] altermagnetic semimetal in which topology, magnetism, and lattice dynamics are intrinsically intertwined. T…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051111] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure and transport properties of the altermagnetic semimetal NiS using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topology, magnetism, and lattice dynamics in NiS, which exhibits altermagnetism and carrier compensation.
method: Combines density-functional theory, Berry-curvature analysis, semiclassical Boltzmann transport, and atomistic spin dynamics.
result: NiS is identified as a compensated altermagnetic semimetal with Dirac topology, anomalous Hall response, and giant magnetoresistance.
conclusion: The material's properties arise from the intrinsic coupling of topology and magnetism, offering a platform for spintronic applications.

title: Mesoscopic Scattering Dynamics Under Generic Uniform Su(2) Gauge Fields: Spin-momentum Relaxation And Coherent Backscattering
authors: Masataka Kakoi, Christian Miniatura, And Keith Slevin

We investigate the time- and momentum-resolved dynamics of matter waves undergoing elastic scattering from a disordered potential in the presence of spatially uniform SU(2) gauge fields. We derive the disorder-averaged density matrix as a function of time and momentum within the weak-localization re…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-momentum relaxation and coherent backscattering of matter waves under SU(2) gauge fields in disordered potentials.
motivation: To understand the interplay between gauge fields and disorder in mesoscopic systems, which is relevant for spintronics and cold atom experiments.
method: The authors derive the disorder-averaged density matrix using weak-localization theory and analyze time- and momentum-resolved dynamics.
result: They find that uniform SU(2) gauge fields modify the coherent backscattering peak and spin relaxation rates.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum transport in the presence of non-Abelian gauge fields, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Percolation-driven Ferromagnetism In A Dilute Magnetic Topological Insulator
authors: Farhan Islam, Santanu Pakhira, Deborah L. Schlagel, Dhurba R. Jaishi, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Thomas Heitmann, David C. Johnston, Robert J. Mcqueeney, And David Vaknin

Single-crystal neutron scattering and magnetic susceptibility measurements of the dilute magnetic topological insulator ([MATH] demonstrate the emergence of long-range ferromagnetic (FM) order below ${T}_{}=12±1{0ex}}\math…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014424] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation-driven ferromagnetism in a dilute magnetic topological insulator using neutron scattering and susceptibility measurements.
motivation: To understand the emergence of long-range ferromagnetic order in a dilute magnetic topological insulator, which is relevant for spintronics and topological quantum computing.
method: Single-crystal neutron scattering and magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on the dilute magnetic topological insulator.
result: Long-range ferromagnetic order emerges below T_C = 12 K, driven by percolation of magnetic moments.
conclusion: The ferromagnetic order in this dilute magnetic topological insulator is percolation-driven, providing insight into magnetic ordering in such systems.

title: Anomalous Diffusion And Effective Shear Modulus In A Semisolid Membrane
authors: Vikash Pandey And Dhrubaditya Mitra
abstract:
Author(s): Vikash Pandey and Dhrubaditya Mitra

From the perspective of physical properties, the cell membrane is an exotic two-dimensional material that has a dual nature: it exhibits characteristics of fluids, i.e., lipid molecules show lateral diffusion, while also demonstrating properties of solids, evidenced by a nonzero shear modulus. We co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014411] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anomalous diffusion and effective shear modulus in a semisolid membrane, focusing on biophysical properties of cell membranes.
motivation: Cell membranes exhibit both fluid and solid properties; understanding their mechanical and diffusive behavior is important for biophysics.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or simulations to analyze diffusion and shear modulus in a semisolid membrane system.
result: The paper reports anomalous diffusion and a nonzero effective shear modulus, characterizing the dual nature of the membrane.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the physical properties of cell membranes, but the work is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Free-fermionic And Free-parafermionic Multispin Quantum Chains With Nonhomogeneous Interacting Ranges
authors: Francisco C. Alcaraz
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco C. Alcaraz

A large family of multispin interacting one-dimensional quantum spin models with [MATH] symmetry and a free-particle eigenspectra are known in the literature. They are free-fermionic ([MATH]) and free-parafermionic ([MATH]) quantum chains. The essential ingredient that implies the free-particle spectr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014146] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies free-fermionic and free-parafermionic multispin quantum chains with nonhomogeneous interaction ranges, focusing on exact solvability and free-particle spectra.
motivation: To generalize known families of exactly solvable quantum spin models with free-particle spectra to cases with nonhomogeneous interaction ranges, which are less understood.
method: The author constructs a family of multispin interacting quantum chains with Z_n symmetry and shows they have free-particle eigenspectra by mapping to free-fermionic or free-parafermionic systems.
result: Exact solutions are obtained for these models, demonstrating free-particle spectra despite nonhomogeneous interactions.
conclusion: The work extends the class of exactly solvable quantum spin chains, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Nonmonotonic Percolation Threshold In Correlated Networks And Hypergraphs
authors: L. D. Valdez And C. E. la Rocca
abstract:
Author(s): L. D. Valdez and C. E. La Rocca

We study the effect of assortative and disassortative mixing on the robustness of networks under random node failures. For ordinary (dyadic) networks, by using the generating function technique and stochastic simulations, we show that the relationship between the Pearson assortativity coefficient $r…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014313] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation thresholds in correlated networks and hypergraphs under random node failures.
motivation: Understanding network robustness is important for real-world systems, but the paper focuses on classical network theory without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use generating function techniques and stochastic simulations to analyze assortative and disassortative mixing effects on percolation thresholds.
result: They find nonmonotonic behavior of the percolation threshold as a function of the correlation parameter.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical network science but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Scaling Laws And Relaxation Rate At First Order Desynchronization
authors: Ayushi Suman And Sarika Jalan
abstract:
Author(s): Ayushi Suman and Sarika Jalan

While divergences in correlation length and time, hallmarks of criticality, have been established for second-order transitions to synchronization in the Kuramoto model, a comprehensive understanding of analogous scalings for abrupt transitions to desynchronization remains elusive. Through simulation…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012202] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling laws and relaxation rates at first-order desynchronization transitions in the Kuramoto model.
motivation: Understanding critical phenomena in synchronization transitions is important, but the paper focuses on classical coupled oscillators without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Numerical simulations of the Kuramoto model are used to analyze scaling behavior near first-order desynchronization.
result: The authors find scaling laws and relaxation rates that differ from second-order transitions.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical synchronization theory but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Self-organized Model For The Flicker Noise In Interacting Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, And Vadood Adami
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, and Vadood Adami

We investigate self-organized criticality in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) by introducing a lattice-based model that incorporates electron-electron interactions through the concept of coherence length. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that in the strongly interacting regime, the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014141] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-organized criticality and flicker noise in a 2D electron gas with electron-electron interactions, using a lattice model and numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding the origin of 1/f noise in interacting electron systems is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A lattice-based model incorporating coherence length to capture electron-electron interactions is simulated numerically to study self-organized criticality.
result: In the strongly interacting regime, the system exhibits self-organized criticality and power-law noise spectra characteristic of flicker noise.
conclusion: The model provides a possible mechanism for flicker noise in 2DEG based on self-organized criticality.

title: Spectral Statistics And Localization Properties Of A ${\mathrm{C}}_{3}$-symmetric Billiard
authors: Matic Orel And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): Matic Orel and Marko Robnik

We revisit the spectral statistics of the [MATH]-symmetric billiard introduced by F. Leyvraz et al. [
tldr: This paper studies spectral statistics and localization properties of a C3-symmetric billiard, showing GOE and GUE statistics depending on symmetry block.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and spectral properties in systems with discrete symmetry, revisiting a known billiard with high-resolution numerical methods.
method: High-precision numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for the C3-symmetric billiard, analyzing level spacing distributions and localization measures.
result: The system exhibits GOE statistics in the symmetric subspace and GUE statistics in the antisymmetric subspace, with intermediate localization behavior.
conclusion: The C3-symmetric billiard provides a clear example of symmetry-induced spectral statistics crossover, relevant to quantum chaos theory.

title: Stability And Interactions Of Hopfions In Confined Chiral Systems: Role Of The Background Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey O. Leonov

We present a systematic study of isolated hopfions in confined layers of chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals with strong surface anchoring and a film thickness fixed to one spiral pitch. We focus on the structure, stability, and interactions of hopfions under these conditions. Using numer…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015416] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hopfions in confined chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals, focusing on their stability and interactions.
motivation: Hopfions are topological solitons that may have applications in spintronics and liquid crystal devices, but their behavior in confined geometries is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations are used to model hopfions in thin films with strong surface anchoring and fixed thickness, analyzing their structure and interactions.
result: The stability and interaction properties of hopfions depend sensitively on the background phase and confinement conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling hopfions in confined systems, which could be relevant for future device applications.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Occupation times are fundamental in stochastic processes, but two-time statistics—which probe temporal correlations and aging—have not been exactly characterized for jump processes.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for the joint distribution of occupation times at two different times for a class of jump processes, using renewal theory and Laplace transform methods.
result: They find that the two-time occupation statistics exhibit aging, meaning the correlation depends on the absolute times, not just the time difference, and deviate from the arcsine law.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, highlighting aging effects that are absent in Brownian motion.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani
abstract:
Author(s): S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, and Maria Cristina Mariani

Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis has emerged as a standard tool for characterizing scale invariance in complex systems, yet its application to discrete spin models is frequently marred by reports of “spurious multifractality” that contradict established theory. In this work, we resolve th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014139] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves spurious multifractality in the 2D Ising model using finite-size scaling.
motivation: Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis often yields spurious multifractality in discrete spin models, contradicting theory.
method: The authors apply finite-size scaling to multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis of the 2D Ising model.
result: They show that apparent multifractality is a finite-size artifact and can be removed by proper scaling.
conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractality in spin models.

title: Phenomenological Renormalization Group In Neuronal Models Near Criticality
authors: Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, And Mauro Copelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, and Mauro Copelli

The phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) has been applied to the study of scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal data, providing evidence for critical phenomena in the brain. However, it remains unclear how reliably these observed signatures indicate genuine critical behavior, as it is not we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014310] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies phenomenological renormalization group to neuronal models to study criticality, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether scale-invariant signatures in neuronal data reliably indicate genuine critical behavior.
method: The authors apply the phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) to neuronal models and analyze the resulting scaling behavior.
result: The PRG method reveals signatures of criticality, but the reliability of these signatures as indicators of genuine critical behavior remains uncertain.
conclusion: The study highlights limitations of PRG in distinguishing criticality from other scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal systems.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper shows that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to demonstrate the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the ordered phase in the Vicsek model does not break O(2) symmetry; instead, the transition is of a different nature.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect, and the model's phase transition requires a different theoretical explanation.

title: Ghost Imaging With Free Electron-photon Pairs
authors: Sergei Bogdanov, Alexander Preimesberger, Harsh Mishra, Dominik Hornof, Thomas Spielauer, Florian Thajer, Max Maurer, Pia Falb, Leo Stöger, Thomas Schachinger, Friedrich Bleicher, Michael S. Seifner, Isobel C. Bicket, And Philipp Haslinger
abstract:
Author(s): Sergei Bogdanov, Alexander Preimesberger, Harsh Mishra, Dominik Hornof, Thomas Spielauer, Florian Thajer, Max Maurer, Pia Falb, Leo Stöger, Thomas Schachinger, Friedrich Bleicher, Michael S. Seifner, Isobel C. Bicket, and Philipp Haslinger

Coincidence imaging, also known as ghost imaging, is a technique that exploits correlations between two particles to reconstruct information about a specimen. The particle that relays the spatial information about the object remains completely noninteracting, while the particle used to probe the obj…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033120] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ghost imaging using correlated free electron-photon pairs, where the electron interacts with the object and the photon carries the spatial information.
motivation: To extend ghost imaging to a new regime using free electrons and photons, potentially enabling imaging with reduced sample damage.
method: The authors generate correlated electron-photon pairs via inverse Compton scattering and use coincidence detection to reconstruct images from the photon signal.
result: They successfully reconstruct images of test objects using only the photon arm, with the electron arm interacting with the object.
conclusion: Ghost imaging with free electron-photon pairs is feasible and may offer advantages for imaging sensitive samples.

title: Quasicrystalline Analog Of The Haldane Model
authors: B. D. K. Burgess And N. R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): B. D. K. Burgess and N. R. Cooper

We present a model for a topological quasicrystalline system that is suitable for realization in cold atom experiments. We define the model in terms of complex momentum-space couplings that break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and detail how it may be experimentally realized using two-photon Raman cou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033105] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quasicrystalline analog of the Haldane model with broken time-reversal symmetry, suitable for cold atom experiments.
motivation: To explore topological phases in quasicrystalline systems, which lack translational symmetry but can exhibit nontrivial topology.
method: The model is defined using complex momentum-space couplings that break time-reversal symmetry, and an experimental realization via two-photon Raman coupling in cold atoms is proposed.
result: The quasicrystalline system supports chiral edge states and a nonzero Chern number, analogous to the Haldane model.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline systems can host topological phases similar to crystalline topological insulators, and the model is experimentally feasible with current cold atom techniques.

title: Position-resolved Resonance Quantization For Lossy Cavities
authors: Lucas Weitzel, Andreas Buchleitner, And Dominik Lentrodt
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Weitzel, Andreas Buchleitner, and Dominik Lentrodt

Modern experiments in resonators are moving to ever more extreme quantum regimes, posing major challenges to established theoretical approaches, such as so-called few-mode models. While these models have driven major insights for traditional regimes, they are now hitting their limitations for highly…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033108] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for resonance quantization in lossy cavities using a position-resolved approach.
motivation: Standard few-mode models fail in extreme quantum regimes of resonators; a more accurate theoretical description is needed.
method: The authors introduce a position-resolved quantization scheme that accounts for cavity losses and mode coupling.
result: They derive quantized resonance modes that incorporate spatial dependence and dissipation, improving upon few-mode approximations.
conclusion: The position-resolved approach provides a more accurate description of quantum optical phenomena in lossy cavities, relevant for cavity QED experiments.

title: Dual Energy-differentiated Topological Transition In Artificial Red Phosphorus Chains
authors: Vít Jakubský, B. Manjarrez-Montañez, Rafael A. Méndez-Sánchez, And Yonatan Betancur-Ocampo
abstract:
Author(s): Vít Jakubský, B. Manjarrez-Montañez, Rafael A. Méndez-Sánchez, and Yonatan Betancur-Ocampo

We investigate the spectral and topological properties of an atomic chain of red phosphorus. We reveal the separation of flat-band states from the rest of the system and calculate its energy bands analytically. The topological properties of the system are established through the evaluation of the Be…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033110] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties of an artificial red phosphorus chain, revealing flat-band separation and energy-differentiated topological transitions.
motivation: To understand the spectral and topological properties of atomic chains of red phosphorus, which may have implications for condensed matter physics.
method: Analytical calculation of energy bands and evaluation of topological invariants (e.g., Berry phase) for the atomic chain model.
result: Flat-band states are separated from the rest of the system, and energy-differentiated topological transitions are identified.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the topological nature of red phosphorus chains but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dimensional Crossover Of Bound Complexes In A Two-species Bose-Hubbard Lattice: Correlations And Dynamics
authors: Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, And Stephanie M. Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, and Stephanie M. Reimann

We study the equilibrium and nonequilibrium formation of four-particle complexes in a balanced two-species Bose-Hubbard model with repulsive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033111] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies four-particle bound complexes in a two-species Bose-Hubbard model using exact diagonalization, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the formation and dynamics of bound complexes in ultracold atomic systems is important for many-body physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Exact diagonalization of a two-species Bose-Hubbard model with repulsive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions.
result: Characterization of the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and tetramer states, and their nonequilibrium formation.
conclusion: The study provides insights into bound complexes in lattice systems, but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Pulsed Optical Injection Steering In Multistable Semiconductor Laser Arrays Under Correlated Noise
authors: Max M. Chumley And Herbert G. Winful
abstract:
Author(s): Max M. Chumley and Herbert G. Winful

We demonstrate robust programmable state preparation in small Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) arrays with optical feedback using transient optical injection in the form of Gaussian pulses. In Lang-Kobayashi-type models of delay-coupled two- and three-laser arrays, multistability gives…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033112] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable state preparation in small VCSEL arrays using pulsed optical injection under correlated noise.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multistable laser arrays for applications in optical computing and communication.
method: Uses Lang-Kobayashi-type models with delay-coupled lasers and transient Gaussian optical injection pulses.
result: Shows that pulsed injection can steer the array into desired states despite correlated noise.
conclusion: Pulsed optical injection is an effective technique for state preparation in small VCSEL arrays.

title: Spin Glass Dynamics On Complex Hardware Topologies: A Bond-correlated Percolation Approach
authors: Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, And Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz
abstract:
Author(s): Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, and Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz

Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is a central problem in statistical physics and quantum annealing. Spin glass models provide a natural framework to explore this connection, as their energy landscapes are governed by competing interactions and constraine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033099] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies using a bond-correlated percolation approach.
motivation: Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is a central problem in statistical physics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors develop a bond-correlated percolation model to analyze spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies.
result: The model captures key features of relaxation and provides insights into the role of topology in spin glass behavior.
conclusion: The bond-correlated percolation approach offers a useful framework for studying spin glass dynamics on complex networks.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, and Alessandro Toschi

By means of cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT), we study how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of the self-consistent perturbation theory in two-dimensional systems and the most relevant physical consequences associated with it, such as the CDMFT Mott transition. To this aim, we…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the associated physical consequences like the Mott transition.
method: The authors employ cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to analyze two-dimensional systems with short-range correlations.
result: They identify nonperturbative effects arising from short-range correlations and their role in the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations have significant nonperturbative effects on the Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to the orbital Hall effect.
motivation: Previous calculations of the orbital magnetic moment omitted a Berry connection term; this work aims to provide a rigorous derivation and assess its impact on the orbital Hall effect.
method: The authors derive matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment including the Berry connection term, and compute the orbital Hall conductivity for a model system.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital Hall conductivity in certain materials, highlighting the need for its inclusion.
conclusion: The corrected orbital magnetic moment formula is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding for phase estimation.
motivation: To optimize quantum simulation for chemical systems by evaluating different encoding and simulation techniques.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other methods in terms of gate count and circuit depth for Hamiltonian simulation.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces resource requirements for certain Hamiltonians but overall contribution is incremental.
conclusion: The paper is a benchmarking study without novel theoretical or algorithmic advances in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in quasiperiodic systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors investigate two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, analyzing the quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and interlayer hybridization effects.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of quasiperiodic lattices but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the SSH model, comparing three diagnostics.
motivation: Topological phases are typically defined at zero temperature, but realistic systems operate at finite temperature, so understanding how topology manifests in mixed states is important.
method: The authors compute the ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body topological invariant for the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension at nonzero temperature.
result: They find that the ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined and captures topological features, while the other diagnostics have limitations.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a useful indicator of topology in mixed states, but the study is specific to non-interacting models and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation For Open Systems: Emergence Of Exceptional Points In Excitonic Spectra From First Principles
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, And Gianluca Stefanucci
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, and Gianluca Stefanucci

Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031020] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems, predicting exceptional points in excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides for non-Hermitian quantum devices.
motivation: To understand and control excitonic properties in open quantum systems for novel optical and valleytronic devices.
method: They develop a non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter equation from first principles to model excitons in open systems coupled to photonic environments.
result: They find that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides.
conclusion: This provides a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang

Theoretical and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031017] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven topological phase transitions in monolayer TaIrTe4 without moiré engineering.
motivation: To explore topological phases in a single naturally layered crystal, avoiding the complexity of moiré systems.
method: Combines theoretical modeling and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe4.
result: Reveals a rich landscape of interaction-driven topological phases.
conclusion: Monolayer TaIrTe4 is a promising platform for studying topological phases without moiré engineering.

title: Limits Of Inference In Complex Systems: When Stochastic Models Become Indistinguishable
authors: Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, And Sandro Azaele
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, and Sandro Azaele

A path-inference framework quantifies data resolution limits that render distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements that maximize information extraction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031015] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path-inference framework to quantify when distinct stochastic models become empirically indistinguishable due to finite data resolution.
motivation: In complex systems, multiple stochastic models may fit observed data equally well, limiting our ability to infer the true underlying dynamics. The authors aim to formalize these limits and provide guidelines for experimental design.
method: The authors propose a path-inference framework based on information theory and stochastic processes, analyzing how data resolution and sample size affect model distinguishability.
result: They derive bounds on the distinguishability of stochastic models and show that finite data resolution can make models empirically equivalent, even if they are theoretically distinct.
conclusion: The framework offers practical guidelines for designing experiments to maximize information extraction and model discrimination in complex systems.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze generalization in deep neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: Understanding generalization in deep learning is a central challenge; the authors aim to derive exact generalization error for a multilayer perceptron.
method: They employ tools from statistical physics (replica method, cavity method) and random matrix theory to analyze a deep fully connected network in the proportional limit.
result: They derive the generalization error and uncover how feature learning propagates across layers, revealing mechanisms governing network behavior near interpolation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical characterization of deep learning generalization using physics-inspired methods, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They incorporate Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The Floquet-based approach significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet engineering can enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a predicted phase of matter but have not been experimentally confirmed; this work aims to provide evidence.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy is used to measure the out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response of a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: An out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response is observed, consistent with a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest that twisted MoTe2 bilayers host a fractional topological insulator, but further confirmation is needed.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical framework for coupling quantum fields to classical spacetime using covariant path integrals.
motivation: To reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable intermediate theory.
method: Develops covariant path integral techniques for quantum fields backreacting on a classical spacetime background.
result: A consistent formalism that describes the backreaction of quantum fields on classical geometry without quantizing gravity.
conclusion: The framework offers a way to test whether spacetime is fundamentally classical or quantum, bridging quantum field theory and general relativity.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how an external electric field modulates interlayer interactions and sliding resistance.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly alter interlayer binding energies and friction forces, enabling tunable sliding resistance.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route for active control of friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: An LLM-based agent automates scientific discovery by exploring and modeling physical systems.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: Uses a large-language model as a generalist agent to iteratively propose experiments, analyze data, and refine models.
result: The agent successfully uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to analyze particle motion.
result: Relaxation is governed by rare events where particles escape from their local cages, leading to cooperative rearrangements.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of rare events in glassy dynamics, providing insight into the nature of the glass transition.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experiment.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity proofs only cover the dilute regime; this work extends the theoretical basis to the experimentally relevant regime.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from random matrix theory and approximate counting.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the linear-mode regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, and provide evidence that the relevant distribution is anti-concentrated.
conclusion: The results validate the hardness of current photonic quantum advantage experiments and provide a rigorous foundation for future demonstrations.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and identifies ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The work contributes to machine learning theory but is unrelated to the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such systems.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Understanding the stability of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to compute the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To predict physical links in networks where causal relationships are not directly observable.
method: Uses a physics-informed approach combining network science and dynamical systems theory.
result: Demonstrates accurate inference of causal links across various networked dynamics.
conclusion: The framework provides a general method for link prediction in complex networks.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing that includes stages from basic quantum advantage to full fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing but does not present new technical results.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is believed to be a classically hard problem that quantum computers can solve efficiently.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility on current hardware.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into potential quantum advantage for topological problems.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Linear system solving is central to machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and linear combination of unitaries.
result: It catalogs the evolution of quantum linear system solvers and their applications in machine learning, differential equations, and optimization.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding magnetic phenomena in 2D materials and their potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on their exotic electronic states and many-body phenomena.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and correlation effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a platform for studying strongly correlated and topological physics, but the paper is primarily a materials science review.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents under a single field-theoretic framework.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion processes.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unified tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to be a rich field with broad applications, and interdisciplinary collaboration remains crucial.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with many open questions, and the review provides a comprehensive guide for researchers.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review presents an outlook on how these models can be incorporated into studies relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need to be better integrated into application-oriented research.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic applications, and understanding their quantum aspects could enable new functionalities.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions.
result: It summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may offer novel functionalities, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review compiles current constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental improvements and theoretical developments are needed.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why clarifies the limits of thermodynamics and enables design of materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of physical properties (e.g., elastic moduli, piezoelectric coefficients) where measured values exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., homogeneity, equilibrium, linearity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made under conditions that violate the assumptions of the bounds, such as using composite materials, non-equilibrium states, or nonlinear effects.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the underlying assumptions, leading to novel material properties without contradicting thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with ultracold atoms, photonics, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to address fundamental questions in physics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and matter-wave interferometry.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence, collapse models, and entanglement mediated by gravity, alongside experimental platforms such as matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics.
result: The review summarizes current theoretical frameworks and experimental progress, highlighting that experiments testing whether gravity causes decoherence or mediates entanglement are underway.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems provide a promising avenue to probe quantum gravity effects, and ongoing experiments will guide future theoretical developments.

title: Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In A Percolative Two-Dimensional Superconductor
authors: Wenjun Liu, Chenghe Wang, Xiubin Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tao Zhang, Xiao-Xiao Zhang, And Jing Li
abstract:
