Author(s): Wenjun Liu, Chenghe Wang, Xiubin Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tao Zhang, Xiao-Xiao Zhang, and Jing Li

Percolative superconductivity frequently arises in two-dimensional van der Waals materials due to reduced dimensionality, enhanced quantum fluctuations, and complex electron-phonon interactions, providing a unique platform where normal electrons coexist with Cooper pairs. We report the observation o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056201] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports observation of third-order nonlinear transport in a percolative two-dimensional superconductor, focusing on transport properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonlinear transport in percolative superconductors where normal electrons coexist with Cooper pairs.
method: Experimental measurement of third-order nonlinear transport in a two-dimensional van der Waals superconductor.
result: Observation of third-order nonlinear transport behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into transport in percolative superconductors but do not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fröhlich-Type Polarons In Isotopically Enriched Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Ioannis Chatzakis, Timur Abdilov, Elliott Walker, Jaime Freitas, Song Liu, And James H. Edgar
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Chatzakis, Timur Abdilov, Elliott Walker, Jaime Freitas, Song Liu, and James H. Edgar

Exciton-phonon interactions play a central role in defining the optical response of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), yet their quantitative determination has remained incomplete. Here, we reveal the Fröhlich-type exciton-phonon coupling in boron-10-enriched hBN using low-temperature cathodoluminescenc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056904] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Fröhlich-type exciton-phonon coupling in isotopically enriched hexagonal boron nitride using low-temperature cathodoluminescence.
motivation: Exciton-phonon interactions are crucial for the optical properties of hBN, but their quantitative determination has been incomplete.
method: Low-temperature cathodoluminescence spectroscopy was performed on boron-10-enriched hBN to measure exciton-phonon coupling.
result: The Fröhlich-type exciton-phonon coupling was revealed and quantified.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative understanding of exciton-phonon interactions in hBN, which is important for its optoelectronic applications.

title: Diffusion In Two-Dimensional Hyperuniform Media
authors: Jing Zhang, Shengda Zhao, Rongxin Yue, Jiaxin Yu, And Xinghua Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Zhang, Shengda Zhao, Rongxin Yue, Jiaxin Yu, and Xinghua Zhang

Understanding diffusion in disordered systems composed of obstacle particles is crucial for elucidating transport phenomena ranging from biological tissues to engineered porous materials. Existing studies predominantly employ the random sequential adsorption method and characterize media solely by d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 057101] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies diffusion in two-dimensional hyperuniform disordered media, focusing on transport properties in classical systems.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in disordered obstacle systems is important for transport in biological tissues and porous materials, but existing studies use limited characterization methods.
method: The authors simulate diffusion in hyperuniform media generated by a specific algorithm and analyze mean squared displacement and effective diffusivity.
result: They find that hyperuniform disorder leads to anomalous diffusion behavior distinct from random or periodic media.
conclusion: The work provides insights into transport in hyperuniform structures but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Coherent Regime Of Kapitza-Dirac Effect With Electrons
authors: Kamila Moriová, Petr Koutenský, Neli Laštovičková Streshkova, Marius Constantin Chirita Mihaila, Zbyněk Šobáň, Jaromír Kopeček, Andreas Schertel, And Martin Kozák
abstract:
Author(s): Kamila Moriová, Petr Koutenský, Neli Laštovičková Streshkova, Marius Constantin Chirita Mihaila, Zbyněk Šobáň, Jaromír Kopeček, Andreas Schertel, and Martin Kozák

Electron matter waves coherently diffract when passing through a periodic structure of light formed by two interfering light waves. In this so-called Kapitza-Dirac effect, the electron momentum changes due to absorption and emission of photons via stimulated Compton scattering. Until now, the effect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053604] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates the coherent Kapitza-Dirac effect with electrons, showing high-contrast diffraction and coherence between diffracted orders.
motivation: To observe and characterize the coherent regime of the Kapitza-Dirac effect, where electrons diffract from a standing light wave via stimulated Compton scattering, and to demonstrate coherence between different momentum orders.
method: The authors use a pulsed laser to create a standing wave grating and direct a beam of electrons through it, measuring the diffraction pattern and interference between diffracted orders.
result: They achieve high-contrast diffraction and observe interference fringes indicating coherence between the diffracted electron beams.
conclusion: The coherent Kapitza-Dirac effect is realized, enabling potential applications in electron interferometry and quantum control of electron beams.

title: Theory Of Angle Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy Of Altermagnetic Mott Insulators
authors: Lorenzo Lanzini, Purnendu Das, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Lanzini, Purnendu Das, and Michael Knap

Altermagnetism has emerged as an unconventional form of collinear magnetism with spatial rotational symmetries, that give rise to strongly spin-split bands despite an underlying fully compensated antiferromagnetic order. Here, we develop a theory for the angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy res…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056501] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory for angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of altermagnetic Mott insulators.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a new collinear magnetic phase with spin-split bands but no net magnetization; understanding its spectroscopic signatures is important for experimental detection.
method: The authors model the electronic structure of altermagnetic Mott insulators and compute the ARPES response using a theoretical framework.
result: They predict distinct spin- and angle-resolved photoemission features that can identify altermagnetic order.
conclusion: The theory provides a basis for interpreting ARPES experiments on altermagnetic materials.

title: Predicting The Energies Of ${\mathrm{Cf}}^{17+}$ For An Optical Clock
authors: S. G. Porsev And M. S. Safronova
abstract:
Author(s): S. G. Porsev and M. S. Safronova

Highly charged ions (HCIs) combine compact electronic structure with strong relativistic effects, offering both robustness against external perturbations and enhanced sensitivity to variations of the fine-structure constant. Recent advances in sympathetic cooling and trapping enable precision measur…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012819] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts atomic energy levels of highly charged Cf^{17+} for optical clock applications.
motivation: Highly charged ions offer robustness and sensitivity for precision measurements, but their complex electronic structure requires accurate theoretical predictions.
method: The authors use relativistic many-body methods, including configuration interaction and coupled-cluster approaches, to compute energy levels.
result: They provide predicted energy levels and transition wavelengths for Cf^{17+} relevant to optical clock design.
conclusion: The predictions support the development of optical clocks based on highly charged ions, but the work is primarily atomic physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Discrete Cavity Dynamics In Free-space Brillouin Laser
authors: Jiabao Peng, Longjie Zhang, Zhenxu Bai, Stephan Fritzsche, And Zhiwei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiabao Peng, Longjie Zhang, Zhenxu Bai, Stephan Fritzsche, and Zhiwei Lu

Highly coherent lasers are central to modern photonics. To date, high-coherence operation has been achieved predominantly in microcavity and fiber-based platforms. More recently, free-space Brillouin-laser experiments have revealed unusually strong noise suppression whose physical origin cannot be e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013520] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise suppression in a free-space Brillouin laser, a topic in laser physics with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the physical origin of unusually strong noise suppression in free-space Brillouin lasers.
method: Theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration of discrete cavity dynamics in a free-space Brillouin laser system.
result: The noise suppression is attributed to discrete cavity dynamics, enabling high-coherence operation.
conclusion: Free-space Brillouin lasers can achieve high coherence through cavity dynamics, but the work is purely classical optics.

title: Quantification Of Parasitic Etalons In Fabry-Perot Cavities And The Errors They Cause In Pound-Drever-Hall Frequency Stabilization Schemes
authors: Malte Misfeldt, Emily Rose Rees, Andrew Wade, David Rabeling, And Kirk Mckenzie
abstract:
Author(s): Malte Misfeldt, Emily Rose Rees, Andrew Wade, David Rabeling, and Kirk McKenzie

The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) scheme is a well-known technique for stabilizing a laser's frequency to a reference length such as an optical cavity. However, if a PDH setup is not carefully designed, one might easily create parasitic etalons, which are caused by back reflections in the optical path. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013521] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes parasitic etalons in Fabry-Perot cavities and their impact on Pound-Drever-Hall frequency stabilization.
motivation: Parasitic etalons can degrade the performance of PDH frequency stabilization, but their effects are not well quantified.
method: The authors model parasitic etalons as additional cavities and derive analytical expressions for the resulting errors in PDH error signals.
result: They quantify the magnitude of frequency offsets and noise introduced by parasitic etalons, showing that even weak etalons can cause significant errors.
conclusion: Careful optical design is necessary to avoid parasitic etalons in PDH setups, and the provided formulas can guide tolerance requirements.

title: Circular Polarization Of Photon Emission Following Resonant Electron Capture Of Lithiumlike Ions With Spin-polarized Electrons
authors: Y. Li, Y. Z. Wang, S. Fritzsche, And Z. W. Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Li, Y. Z. Wang, S. Fritzsche, and Z. W. Wu

The authors reveal that the circular polarization of x-rays radiated following resonant electron capture in lithiumlike ions is highly sensitive to the spin polarization state of the recombined electrons. This sensitivity provides a diagnostic scheme for spin-polarized electron beams, which proves more promising than the scheme based on linear polarization, owing to a substantially higher efficiency in transferring electron spin polarization into photon circular polarization.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010803] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular polarization of x-rays from resonant electron capture in lithiumlike ions as a diagnostic for spin-polarized electron beams.
motivation: To develop a sensitive diagnostic scheme for spin-polarized electron beams using photon polarization.
method: Theoretical analysis of resonant electron capture in lithiumlike ions with spin-polarized electrons, calculating circular polarization of emitted x-rays.
result: Circular polarization is highly sensitive to electron spin polarization, offering higher efficiency than linear polarization schemes.
conclusion: The proposed diagnostic scheme is promising for measuring spin polarization of electron beams.

title: Nonmonotonic $Q$-factor Evolution Of Flatband Modes In Disordered Finite Moiré Photonic Crystals
authors: Qian Liu, Junjie Wang, Luyao Zhang, Xiang Yao, Xianggao Wang, Peilong Hong, And Yi Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Liu, Junjie Wang, Luyao Zhang, Xiang Yao, Xianggao Wang, Peilong Hong, and Yi Liang

This study investigates radiative loss within a finite, single-cell 3D moiré photonic crystal—the fundamental building block for practical moiré devices. The authors demonstrate a counterintuitive, nonmonotonic dependence of the average quality factor on disorder strength. Specifically, they reveal that weak disorder actively suppresses radiative coupling to enhance the quality factor, whereas stronger disorder exacerbates scattering into the radiation light cone, severely degrading optical confinement.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011503] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonmonotonic evolution of the quality factor in disordered finite moiré photonic crystals, focusing on radiative loss in photonic structures.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects optical confinement in moiré photonic crystals is important for practical photonic devices, but the topic is far from quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze a finite single-cell 3D moiré photonic crystal, calculating the average quality factor as a function of disorder strength.
result: Weak disorder surprisingly enhances the quality factor by suppressing radiative coupling, while stronger disorder degrades it due to increased scattering into the radiation light cone.
conclusion: The work reveals a counterintuitive effect in photonic crystals but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbital-spin Conversion In Solid High-order Harmonic Generation By Ring Configurations
authors: Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, And Jianghua Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, and Jianghua Luo

We theoretically investigate the interaction between azimuthal vector vortex beams and a segmented ring medium, revealing orbital-to-spin conversion in strong-field high-order harmonic generation. We show that engineered gaps in the ring target break the light-matter symmetry and mediate the transfe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013122] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital-to-spin conversion in high-order harmonic generation using vector vortex beams and segmented ring targets.
motivation: To understand and control the transfer of orbital angular momentum to spin angular momentum in strong-field light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical investigation using azimuthal vector vortex beams interacting with a segmented ring medium, with engineered gaps to break symmetry.
result: Orbital-to-spin conversion is observed in high-order harmonic generation, mediated by the broken symmetry from the gaps.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for angular momentum conversion in nonlinear optics, with potential applications in ultrafast optics and light-matter control.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, and Agustin Palacios-Laloy

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a zero-field metastable helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer.
motivation: Understanding the origins of noise in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving their sensitivity, but the paper focuses on a specific sensor technology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental characterization of the noise sources in a single-beam vector magnetometer based on metastable helium-4.
result: They identify the main noise origins and achieve vector magnetic readings with noise below 300 fT/Hz^{1/2} in the optimal regime.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the noise mechanisms of this type of magnetometer, which may aid in sensor optimization.

title: Dimensional And Doping Stability Of Peierls Charge Density Waves In Arrays Of Coupled One-dimensional Chains
authors: Aitor Garcia-Ruiz (艾飛宇), Che-Pin Hsu (許哲彬), Ming-Hao Liu (劉明豪), And Marcin Mucha-Kruczynski
abstract:
Author(s): Aitor Garcia-Ruiz (艾飛宇), Che-Pin Hsu (許哲彬), Ming-Hao Liu (劉明豪), and Marcin Mucha-Kruczynski

The Peierls instability, the spontaneous dimerization of a one-dimensional metallic chain at half-filling, is a paradigmatic mechanism for charge-density-wave (CDW) formation. Here, we test its robustness under finite doping and interchain hybridization in finite-thickness arrays of identical chains…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024110] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of Peierls charge density waves in coupled one-dimensional chains under doping and interchain hybridization.
motivation: To test the robustness of the Peierls instability, a paradigmatic mechanism for CDW formation, in finite-thickness arrays of chains.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical calculations to analyze the effects of finite doping and interchain coupling on the CDW state.
result: They find that the Peierls CDW is stable only under specific conditions and is suppressed by doping or strong interchain hybridization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dimensional and doping stability of CDWs in quasi-1D systems.

title: Intrinsic And Extrinsic Dual-component Evolution Of Electronic Transport In A Magnetic Weyl Semimetal
authors: Yiting Feng, Meng Lyu, Jinying Yang, Shen Zhang, Yibo Wang, Qiusa Ren, Binbin Wang, Hongxiang Wei, Baogen Shen, And Enke Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiting Feng, Meng Lyu, Jinying Yang, Shen Zhang, Yibo Wang, Qiusa Ren, Binbin Wang, Hongxiang Wei, Baogen Shen, and Enke Liu

[MATH], a magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting significant anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Hall angle (AHA) over a wide temperature range, provides an excellent platform for tuning and revealing the rules of the intrinsic and extrinsic contributions t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045131] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intrinsic and extrinsic contributions to anomalous Hall effect in a magnetic Weyl semimetal.
motivation: To understand the transport mechanisms in magnetic Weyl semimetals, which exhibit large anomalous Hall conductivity.
method: Experimental measurements of Hall conductivity and resistivity over a wide temperature range, analyzed using a two-component model separating intrinsic and extrinsic contributions.
result: Identified distinct temperature dependencies of intrinsic (Berry curvature) and extrinsic (skew scattering, side jump) contributions to the anomalous Hall effect.
conclusion: The findings reveal the interplay between intrinsic and extrinsic mechanisms, providing insights into transport in topological semimetals.

title: Asymmetric Scattering Induced Néel Spin-orbit Torque In Antiferromagnets
authors: Sayan Sarkar And Amit Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Sarkar and Amit Agarwal

Magnetic switching in antiferromagnets relies on Néel spin-orbit torque (NSOT), which originates from an electric-field-induced staggered spin polarization of itinerant electrons. In collinear antiferromagnets, such a response requires the spin susceptibility to be odd under combined space-time inve…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045434] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Néel spin-orbit torque in antiferromagnets induced by asymmetric scattering, focusing on magnetic switching in condensed matter physics.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic switching in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic devices, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the staggered spin susceptibility and Néel spin-orbit torque in collinear antiferromagnets under an electric field, using a scattering approach.
result: They find that asymmetric scattering can generate a sizable Néel spin-orbit torque, enabling efficient switching of the Néel vector.
conclusion: The work advances antiferromagnetic spintronics but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: $d$-wave Surface Altermagnetism In Centrosymmetric Collinear Antiferromagnets
authors: Ersoy Şaşıoğlu, Ingrid Mertig, And Samir Lounis
abstract:
Author(s): Ersoy Şaşıoğlu, Ingrid Mertig, and Samir Lounis

Broken inversion symmetry at the surfaces of centrosymmetric collinear antiferromagnets lifts the combined inversion and time-reversal symmetry ([MATH]) and can enable nonrelativistic [MATH]-wave spin splitting, termed surface altermagnetism. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface altermagnetism in centrosymmetric collinear antiferromagnets, a condensed matter physics topic unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how broken inversion symmetry at surfaces can enable nonrelativistic d-wave spin splitting in antiferromagnets.
method: Combines symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations to predict surface altermagnetism.
result: Surface altermagnetism is predicted in centrosymmetric collinear antiferromagnets, leading to d-wave spin splitting.
conclusion: Surface altermagnetism provides a new mechanism for spin splitting in antiferromagnets, relevant for spintronics but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phonon Dynamics Framework For Large-scale Atomistic Simulation
authors: Xingyue Ma, Ming-Hui Lu, Di Wu, And Yurong Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingyue Ma, Ming-Hui Lu, Di Wu, and Yurong Yang

A phonon dynamics framework for atomistic simulation is proposed for studying large-scale system with accuracy comparable to first-principles methods. In this framework, atomic dynamics are reformulated in terms of phonon degrees of freedom, where the localized phonon modes are derived from the phon…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014108] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A phonon dynamics framework for large-scale atomistic simulation with first-principles accuracy.
motivation: To enable accurate atomistic simulations of large systems beyond the reach of first-principles methods.
method: Reformulates atomic dynamics in terms of localized phonon modes derived from the phonon spectrum.
result: The framework achieves accuracy comparable to first-principles methods while allowing simulation of larger systems.
conclusion: The proposed phonon dynamics framework is a promising approach for large-scale atomistic simulations.

title: Multiple Spin-flop Transitions And Magnetoelectric Coupling In Co-substituted ${\mathrm{CuCrP}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$
authors: Dingyu Li, Donger Cheng, Ziyi Zhou, Shuixian Qu, Wenhao Li, Jiaqiang Wang, Qisheng Jiang, Juping Xu, Wu Xie, Ping Miao, Wen Yin, Xinzhi Liu, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Dingyu Li, Donger Cheng, Ziyi Zhou, Shuixian Qu, Wenhao Li, Jiaqiang Wang, Qisheng Jiang, Juping Xu, Wu Xie, Ping Miao, Wen Yin, Xinzhi Liu, and Yue Zheng

We report the synthesis and comprehensive investigation of [MATH] (CCCPS) single crystals and powder samples, a substituted derivative of the van der Waals multiferroic [MATH] (CCPS) w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034117] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports synthesis and characterization of Co-substituted CuCrP2S6, focusing on multiple spin-flop transitions and magnetoelectric coupling.
motivation: To explore the effects of cobalt substitution on the magnetic and multiferroic properties of the van der Waals material CuCrP2S6.
method: Single crystals and powder samples were synthesized, and comprehensive measurements including magnetization, specific heat, and neutron diffraction were performed.
result: Multiple spin-flop transitions were observed, and magnetoelectric coupling was characterized.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic phase diagram and multiferroic behavior of the substituted compound.

title: Correlation-driven Lattice Anharmonicity And Anomalous Thermal Transport In The Kagome Metal ${\mathrm{CaCu}}_{5}$
authors: Tongrui Li, Zhicheng Jiang, Peng Wu, Jian Yuan, Jie Sun, Lidong Zhang, Zhengtai Liu, Yanfeng Guo, Dawei Shen, And Zhe Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Tongrui Li, Zhicheng Jiang, Peng Wu, Jian Yuan, Jie Sun, Lidong Zhang, Zhengtai Liu, Yanfeng Guo, Dawei Shen, and Zhe Sun

Lattice thermal transport in metals is traditionally described under the assumption that a highly mobile electron gas efficiently screens ionic displacements, resulting in a predominantly harmonic interatomic potential. Here, we show that strong electron-electron correlations can profoundly disrupt …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045128] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies lattice anharmonicity and thermal transport in a kagome metal, focusing on electron correlation effects.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in strongly correlated metals is important for fundamental physics and applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and first-principles calculations to investigate electronic structure and lattice dynamics.
result: They find that strong electron-electron correlations drive lattice anharmonicity, leading to anomalous thermal transport behavior.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of correlations in thermal transport but remains within condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Structural Frustration And $p$-orbital Mott Physics In Intrinsically Magnetic Superhard Carbon Nitride Frameworks
authors: Haoyu Liu, Erjun Kan, Yan Qian, And Haiping Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Erjun Kan, Yan Qian, and Haiping Wu

The simultaneous realization of intrinsic magnetism and superhardness within a single light-element lattice represents a fundamental paradox, as the strong [MATH] covalency required for rigidity inherently suppresses the localized moments essential for magnetic ordering. Here, we resolve this di…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014107] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the theoretical prediction of intrinsic magnetism and superhardness in carbon nitride frameworks via p-orbital Mott physics and structural frustration.
motivation: To resolve the paradox that strong covalency in light-element materials suppresses magnetic ordering, aiming to realize both intrinsic magnetism and superhardness simultaneously.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to study electronic structure and magnetic properties of carbon nitride frameworks.
result: The proposed carbon nitride frameworks exhibit both superhardness and intrinsic magnetism due to p-orbital Mott physics and structural frustration.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new class of materials combining superhardness and magnetism, with potential applications in spintronics and high-pressure environments.

title: Particlelike And Wavelike Behavior Of Phonons In ${\mathrm{Cs}}_{2}\mathrm{AgIn}{X}_{6}$ $(X=\mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Br})$ Perovskites: How Rattling Vibrations And Octahedral Rotations Govern Thermal Transport
authors: Ran Zhou, Hongliang Shi, And Yifeng Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Ran Zhou, Hongliang Shi, and Yifeng Duan

Conventional Peierls theory cannot fully capture the thermal transport in strongly anharmonic compounds (e.g., lead-free halide double perovskites) because it does not account for the significant wavelike behavior of phonons—a consequence of their inherent capability to interfere and tunnel. Here, w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014318] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport in lead-free halide double perovskites, focusing on phonon behavior and rattling vibrations.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in strongly anharmonic compounds is important for thermoelectric applications, but conventional Peierls theory fails to capture wavelike phonon behavior.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and Boltzmann transport equation with coherent phonon contributions to model thermal conductivity.
result: They find that rattling vibrations and octahedral rotations lead to significant wavelike phonon transport, enhancing thermal conductivity beyond classical predictions.
conclusion: The study highlights the need to include wavelike phonon effects for accurate thermal transport modeling in anharmonic perovskites.

title: Nonequilibrium Pathways Between Cluster Morphologies In Active Phase Separation: Necking, Rupture, And Cavitation
authors: Liheng Yao (姚立衡), Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Liheng Yao (姚立衡), Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

In a two-dimensional active lattice gas that undergoes motility-induced phase separation, the authors investigate a morphological transition between a system-spanning slab morphology and a compact droplet. They find that the transition from droplet to slab follows a similar mechanism to its equilibrium counterpart, but the reverse transition depends on rare nonequilibrium fluctuations.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014148] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies morphological transitions in active phase separation of an active lattice gas, focusing on nonequilibrium pathways between slab and droplet morphologies.
motivation: Understanding morphological transitions in active matter is important for controlling self-organization in nonequilibrium systems.
method: Simulations of a two-dimensional active lattice gas with motility-induced phase separation, analyzing transition pathways and rare fluctuations.
result: The droplet-to-slab transition follows an equilibrium-like mechanism, while the reverse transition depends on rare nonequilibrium fluctuations leading to necking, rupture, or cavitation.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium pathways dominate the reverse morphological transition, highlighting the role of rare fluctuations in active phase separation.

title: Quiescent And Traveling Solitons In The Fractional Parametrically Driven Damped Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
authors: Dongdong Wang, Rujiang Li, David Laroze, Boris A. Malomed, And Pengfei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Dongdong Wang, Rujiang Li, David Laroze, Boris A. Malomed, and Pengfei Li

We systematically investigate the existence, stability, and dynamics of optical solitons in the framework of the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with the Riesz-fractional diffraction operator, cubic self-focusing, and linear loss, balanced by a linear parametric drive. The model, whic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014223] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies solitons in a fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with parametric driving and damping, which is a topic in nonlinear optics and fractional dynamics.
motivation: To understand the existence and stability of solitons in systems with fractional diffraction, which has applications in optics and condensed matter.
method: The authors use analytical approximations and numerical simulations to find quiescent and traveling soliton solutions and analyze their stability.
result: They identify regions of stable solitons and characterize their dynamics, including the effect of fractional order on soliton properties.
conclusion: The fractional parametric drive can support stable solitons, and the fractional order significantly influences soliton behavior.

title: Survival Probability Of Particles Inside The Lemon Billiard
authors: Daniel Borin, Edson Denis Leonel, And Diego Fregolent Mendes de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borin, Edson Denis Leonel, and Diego Fregolent Mendes de Oliveira

We study the escape of particles in the lemon billiard, a two-parameter family of billiard systems defined by the intersection of two identical circles. Using numerical simulations, we explore how the survival probability depends on the position and size of the hole, as well as on the billiard shape…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014224] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies particle escape dynamics in a classical lemon billiard using numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding survival probability in chaotic billiards is a fundamental problem in classical dynamical systems.
method: Numerical simulations of particle trajectories in the lemon billiard with varying hole positions and sizes.
result: Survival probability depends sensitively on hole geometry and billiard shape.
conclusion: The study provides insights into escape dynamics but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Intermittent Motility Of A Synthetic Active Particle In Changing Environments
authors: Rudra Sekhri, Rahil N. Valani, And Tapio Simula
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra Sekhri, Rahil N. Valani, and Tapio Simula

We experimentally investigate the dynamics of synthetic active particles composed of gravitationally bouncing, superwalking droplets confined within an annular fluid bath. Driven by a topologically pumping dual-frequency waveform, the droplets exhibit alternating active (walking) and dormant (bounci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013103] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the intermittent motility of synthetic active particles (bouncing droplets) in changing environments.
motivation: Understanding how active particles adapt to environmental changes is important for designing autonomous microswimmers and understanding biological motility.
method: Experiments with gravitationally bouncing superwalking droplets in an annular fluid bath driven by a dual-frequency waveform, observing transitions between active walking and dormant bouncing states.
result: The droplets exhibit intermittent motility with alternating active and dormant phases, and the dynamics depend on the driving waveform and environmental parameters.
conclusion: The system provides a controlled platform to study active matter and motility in fluctuating environments, but the work is primarily experimental and phenomenological.

title: Unbiased Randomization Of Weighted Bipartite Networks With Exact Degree And Strength Sequences
authors: G. Glaviano And S. Miccichè
abstract:
Author(s): G. Glaviano and S. Miccichè

In the context of complex networks, designing a null model that preserves certain properties of the original network is a fundamental problem. While for binary bipartite networks, the problem has been solved by the curveball algorithm, which preserves the degree of each node exactly, for weighted bi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014312] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm for randomizing weighted bipartite networks while preserving exact degree and strength sequences.
motivation: Null models that preserve network properties are essential for detecting significant structural patterns, but existing methods for weighted bipartite networks are limited.
method: The authors extend the curveball algorithm to weighted bipartite networks, introducing a randomization procedure that exactly preserves both node degrees and strengths.
result: The algorithm is validated on synthetic and real-world networks, showing it efficiently generates unbiased randomized ensembles.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a useful tool for network analysis, but it is purely a computational network science technique with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Partitioning Law Of Polymer Chains Into Flexible Polymer Networks
authors: Haruki Takarai, Takashi Yasuda, Naoyuki Sakumichi, And Takamasa Sakai
abstract:
Author(s): Haruki Takarai, Takashi Yasuda, Naoyuki Sakumichi, and Takamasa Sakai

The equilibrium partitioning of linear polymer chains into flexible polymer networks is governed by intricate entropic constraints arising from the configurational degrees of freedom of both chains and networks; however, a quantitative understanding remains elusive. Using model hydrogels with precis…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015420] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the equilibrium partitioning of linear polymer chains into flexible polymer networks using model hydrogels.
motivation: Understanding the entropic constraints governing polymer partitioning is important for applications like drug delivery and tissue engineering.
method: The authors use model hydrogels with precise network structures and combine experiments with theoretical modeling.
result: They derive a quantitative law describing how polymer chain length and network mesh size affect partitioning.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental understanding of polymer partitioning, which can guide the design of hydrogel-based materials.

title: Underlying Framework Of Structural Decay In Binary Hard-sphere Mixtures
authors: Sławomir Pieprzyk And Arkadiusz C. Brańka
abstract:
Author(s): Sławomir Pieprzyk and Arkadiusz C. Brańka

In liquid mixtures, changes in structural decay have been observed in particle simulations and experiments, and are an important element of their analysis. The work presents a comprehensive description of the long-range behavior of structural pair correlation functions of binary hard-sphere (BHS) mi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015423] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural decay in binary hard-sphere mixtures using pair correlation functions.
motivation: Understanding long-range behavior of structural correlations in liquid mixtures is important for analyzing their properties.
method: The authors provide a comprehensive description of the asymptotic decay of pair correlation functions in binary hard-sphere mixtures.
result: They identify the underlying framework governing structural decay in these mixtures.
conclusion: The work offers a detailed theoretical analysis of structural correlations in hard-sphere mixtures, relevant to liquid state theory.

title: Role Of Manifolds In The Transport Of Chaotic Trajectories In The Standard Nontwist Map
authors: Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, And José Danilo Szezech, Jr.
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, and José Danilo Szezech, Jr.

A crucial question in transport theory is determining the critical parameter values at which abrupt changes in phase space occur. In nontwist Hamiltonian systems, this transition is associated with the breakup of the shearless curve. Ideally, once this curve is destroyed, chaotic trajectories should…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014222] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transport of chaotic trajectories in the standard nontwist map, focusing on the role of manifolds and shearless curve breakup.
motivation: Understanding abrupt changes in phase space transport in nontwist Hamiltonian systems is crucial for transport theory.
method: Numerical simulations and analysis of invariant manifolds in the standard nontwist map.
result: Identified critical parameter values where shearless curve breakup leads to enhanced chaotic transport.
conclusion: Manifold analysis provides insight into transport barriers and their destruction in nontwist systems.

title: Statistical Theory Of Electronic Degrees Of Freedom In Wave Packet Molecular Dynamics
authors: Daniel Plummer, Pontus Svensson, Wiktor Jasniak, Patrick Hollebon, Sam M. Vinko, And Gianluca Gregori
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Plummer, Pontus Svensson, Wiktor Jasniak, Patrick Hollebon, Sam M. Vinko, and Gianluca Gregori

We derive statistical distributions for the degrees of freedom in wave packet molecular dynamics models. Specifically, a theory is developed for the width distributions of Gaussian wave packets in both isotropic and anisotropic formulations. The resulting distribution functions show good agreement w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015219] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives statistical distributions for Gaussian wave packet widths in molecular dynamics models, focusing on electronic degrees of freedom.
motivation: To provide a theoretical foundation for the width parameters in wave packet molecular dynamics, which are often treated empirically.
method: The authors develop statistical theories for isotropic and anisotropic Gaussian wave packet width distributions and compare them with simulations.
result: The derived distribution functions show good agreement with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work offers a statistical framework for understanding electronic degrees of freedom in wave packet molecular dynamics, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Inferring Partial Crystalline Order In Liquids From Electrical Resistivity
authors: Nadine Wetta And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Nadine Wetta and Jean-Christophe Pain

This work investigates how locally persistent crystal-like ordering in liquids influences the Debye-Waller factor. We have developed a theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory which introduces a phonon relaxation time, expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015220] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how crystal-like ordering in liquids affects the Debye-Waller factor using liquid-phonon theory.
motivation: Understanding the influence of local crystalline order on liquid properties is important for condensed matter physics.
method: A theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory is developed, introducing a phonon relaxation time expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear modulus.
result: The framework predicts changes in the Debye-Waller factor due to persistent crystal-like ordering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical approach to infer partial crystalline order in liquids from electrical resistivity measurements.

title: Role Of Stall Forces And Entropic Barriers In Geometry-dependent Polymer Translocation
authors: Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, And Sanjay Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, and Sanjay Kumar

We investigate the role of stall forces and entropic barriers in geometry-dependent polymer translocation through narrow pores. We consider two distinct geometrical constraints: forced translocation through a small pore in a flat membrane separating two semi-infinite three-dimensional spaces, and tr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015419] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polymer translocation through narrow pores under different geometrical constraints, focusing on stall forces and entropic barriers.
motivation: Understanding how geometry affects polymer translocation is important for biological and nanotechnological applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze forced translocation through a flat membrane and a conical pore.
result: They find that stall forces and entropic barriers play a key role in geometry-dependent translocation dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the physics of polymer transport through confined geometries.

title: Amplitude Death And Phase-locked Oscillations In Delay-coupled Oscillators With Frequency Mismatch And Nonisochronism
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

This paper presents an investigation of amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch. These oscillators exhibit nonisochronism, in which the rotation velocities depend on amplitudes. We provide a simple procedure to numerically obta…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014221] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch and nonisochronism.
motivation: Understanding synchronization phenomena in coupled oscillators is important for various fields, but this work focuses on classical nonlinear dynamics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors provide a numerical procedure to obtain amplitude death and phase-locked oscillation regions for delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators.
result: They characterize how frequency mismatch and nonisochronism affect the onset of amplitude death and phase-locked states.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theory of coupled oscillators but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stokes-Einstein-like Scaling Across Fluidized And Caged Transport Regimes In A Driven Complex Plasma
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, and Cătălin M. Ticoş

The Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation links microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic dissipation. Whether it survives in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium remains an open question. Using a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, we isolate therm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015215] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stokes-Einstein relation in a driven complex plasma, which is a classical non-equilibrium system unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether the Stokes-Einstein relation holds in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium.
method: Experimental observation of a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, analyzing microscopic fluctuations and macroscopic dissipation.
result: The Stokes-Einstein-like scaling is observed across fluidized and caged transport regimes.
conclusion: The Stokes-Einstein relation can survive in driven-dissipative systems, but the work is purely classical and does not involve quantum effects or information theory.

title: Large Earthquakes Follow Highly Unequal Ones
authors: Sudip Sarkar And Soumyajyoti Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Sudip Sarkar and Soumyajyoti Biswas

It was conjectured for a long time that the tectonic plates are in a self-organized state of criticality and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of that. It was recently shown that for a system near criticality, the inequality of their responses due to external driving would sharply ri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014143] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies inequality of earthquake magnitudes as a signature of criticality in tectonic plates, using a fiber bundle model.
motivation: To test the conjecture that tectonic plates are in a self-organized critical state and that the Gutenberg-Richter law reflects this, by examining inequality in earthquake magnitudes.
method: The authors analyze earthquake catalog data and use a fiber bundle model to show that large earthquakes are preceded by highly unequal magnitude distributions.
result: They find that large earthquakes follow periods of high inequality in earthquake magnitudes, consistent with critical point behavior.
conclusion: Inequality measures can serve as a precursor for large earthquakes, supporting the self-organized criticality hypothesis for tectonic plates.

title: Dynamics-induced Activity Patterns Of Active-inactive Clusters In Complex Networks
authors: Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

Synchrony patterns describe network states in which nodes of a coupled dynamical system are grouped into clusters based on synchronization between nodes. Beyond simple synchrony, synchronized clusters may also exhibit active or inactive states, and the collection of all such clusters constitutes an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014219] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchrony patterns and active-inactive cluster dynamics in complex networks, focusing on network science and nonlinear dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how synchronized clusters in coupled dynamical systems can exhibit active or inactive states is important for network dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of coupled oscillators on complex networks, identifying conditions for active-inactive cluster patterns.
result: They find that network topology and coupling strength determine the emergence and stability of such activity patterns.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of synchrony in complex networks but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Multiphoton Ionization Driven By Quantum Light
authors: V. P. Kosheleva, S. Panahiyan, A. Rubio, And F. Schlawin
abstract:
Author(s): V. P. Kosheleva, S. Panahiyan, A. Rubio, and F. Schlawin

We present a first-principles [MATH]-matrix framework for multiphoton ionization driven by arbitrary quantum states of light, retaining the full spatial structure of the light fields. Within this framework, we show that the utilization of momentum-entangled photon pairs emitted by ultrathin nonlinear c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033106] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for multiphoton ionization driven by quantum light, focusing on momentum-entangled photon pairs from nonlinear crystals.
motivation: To understand how quantum properties of light, such as entanglement, can enhance multiphoton ionization processes beyond classical light sources.
method: The authors develop a first-principles S-matrix framework that incorporates the full spatial structure of arbitrary quantum states of light.
result: They show that momentum-entangled photon pairs can significantly enhance ionization yields compared to classical light of the same intensity.
conclusion: Quantum light offers a new control knob for strong-field ionization, with potential applications in ultrafast spectroscopy and quantum optics.

title: Enhancing Optically Induced Intersite Spin Transfer In Antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic Ultrathin Films
authors: Ming-Shian Tsai, Li-Han Chang, Chun-Chia Tseng, Kunchala Ramesh Babu, Guang-Yu Guo, Bo-Yao Wang, And Ming-Chang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Shian Tsai, Li-Han Chang, Chun-Chia Tseng, Kunchala Ramesh Babu, Guang-Yu Guo, Bo-Yao Wang, and Ming-Chang Chen

Antiferromagnetic (AFM) films play a crucial role in advanced spintronic devices by regulating adjacent ferromagnetic (FM) layers via interfacial exchange coupling. However, the impact of antiferromagnets on magnetic dynamics of FM films under ultrashort laser pulses remains largely unknown. Using u…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033114] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optically induced spin transfer in antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic ultrathin films, focusing on spintronic device applications.
motivation: Understanding how antiferromagnetic layers affect magnetic dynamics in ferromagnetic films under ultrafast laser pulses is crucial for advanced spintronic devices.
method: The authors use ultrafast laser pulses to induce spin transfer in AFM/FM bilayer films and measure the resulting magnetic dynamics.
result: They find that the antiferromagnetic layer enhances the optically induced intersite spin transfer, leading to faster and more efficient magnetization switching.
conclusion: The results demonstrate a new mechanism for controlling magnetization dynamics in spintronic devices using antiferromagnetic layers.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce and analytically solve a population model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size.
result: Exact solutions are obtained for the population dynamics, revealing how noise and cell-size regulation shape growth.
conclusion: The model provides a tractable framework for studying stochastic exponential growth in cellular populations.

title: Predicting Liquid Properties And Behavior Via Droplet Pinch-off And Machine Learning
authors: Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, And José Rafael Castrejón-Pita
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, and José Rafael Castrejón-Pita

A powerful method allows hard to measure properties like viscosity and surface tension to be determined from a single, high-speed snapshot.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031021] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning on droplet pinch-off images to predict liquid properties like viscosity and surface tension.
motivation: Measuring liquid properties such as viscosity and surface tension is often difficult and requires specialized equipment; a simpler method is needed.
method: High-speed imaging captures droplet pinch-off dynamics, and a machine learning model is trained to predict properties from the images.
result: The method accurately predicts viscosity and surface tension from a single snapshot, demonstrating a practical application of fluid dynamics and ML.
conclusion: This approach offers a powerful, low-cost tool for characterizing liquids, with potential industrial applications.

title: Deceleration Of Accelerator-Produced And In-Trap Electron Cooling Of Highly Charged Ions
authors: S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, And D. Zisis
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, and D. Zisis

The electron cooling of highly charged ions (HCI) in a Penning trap, as well as the deceleration and trapping of accelerator-produced HCI, has been demonstrated at the HITRAP facility, paving the way for unprecedented precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031022] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates deceleration and electron cooling of highly charged ions in a Penning trap at the HITRAP facility.
motivation: To enable high-precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics by producing slow, cold highly charged ions.
method: Accelerator-produced highly charged ions are decelerated and trapped in a Penning trap, then cooled via electron cooling.
result: Successful demonstration of deceleration and in-trap electron cooling of highly charged ions.
conclusion: The HITRAP facility can now provide slow, cold highly charged ions for precision experiments.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical data-analysis tool for extracting quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport in disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials often yields chaotic interpretations; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors develop a theoretical data-analysis tool that resolves ambiguities in nonlinear transport data, enabling extraction of geometric third-order nonlinear transport coefficients.
result: The tool provides a systematic way to identify quantum geometric contributions from experimental data, clarifying the role of disorder.
conclusion: This work offers a practical framework for analyzing nonlinear transport in disordered systems, linking experimental data to quantum geometry.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper engineers molecular clock transitions in heavy polar molecules to suppress electromagnetic noise for precision measurements of physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: To enable high-sensitivity searches for new physics by reducing disruptive electromagnetic noise in molecular clock transitions.
method: Engineered special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules that suppress electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving sensitivity.
result: Demonstrated suppression of electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude in engineered molecular clock transitions.
conclusion: Engineered molecular clock transitions offer a promising route for precision measurements to probe physics beyond the standard model.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré materials is important for potential applications in information manipulation, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering spin moiré superstructures, but does not directly contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision finding in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices, which is important for superconducting electronics.
method: Local protonic gating is applied to InAs homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect while preserving time-reversal symmetry.
result: The authors observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect without an external magnetic field, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes in gate-defined homojunctions, with potential applications in low-power electronics.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transition of the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel magnetic phase transition in a kagome ice compound, contributing to the understanding of frustrated magnetism.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands are of interest for strongly correlated electron physics, but their realization at room temperature is rare. The authors aim to demonstrate a tunable platform for such states.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to probe the electronic structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and stable at room temperature were observed.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states at ambient conditions.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities induce forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping and sorting.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications, including trapping, sorting, and pulling forces.
conclusion: The field has broad applications but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and its implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental observations, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with potential for groundbreaking applications.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium defines active matter as a subset of nonequilibrium systems and reviews recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its definition and scope.
method: The authors provide a historical survey and propose a definition based on energy consumption at the particle level, distinguishing active matter from other nonequilibrium systems.
result: They offer a precise definition and discuss emerging subfields such as quantum active matter.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems, and the proposed definition helps unify the field.

title: Breakthrough In Short-Wavelength Infrared Quantum Efficiency In Te-Hyperdoped Silicon Photodetectors Via Light-Trapping Strategies
authors: E. García-Hemme, R. Benítez-Fernández, S. Duarte-Cano, F. Pérez-Zenteno, S. Algaidy, C. Mata-Alonso, S. de Castro-Romero, R. García-Hernansanz, J. Olea, A. Del Prado, E. San Andrés, I. Mártil, And D. Pastor
abstract:
Author(s): E. García-Hemme, R. Benítez-Fernández, S. Duarte-Cano, F. Pérez-Zenteno, S. Algaidy, C. Mata-Alonso, S. de Castro-Romero, R. García-Hernansanz, J. Olea, A. del Prado, E. San Andrés, I. Mártil, and D. Pastor

A new light-trapping architecture could lead to CMOS-compatible night-vision technology.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 057002] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a breakthrough in short-wavelength infrared quantum efficiency in Te-hyperdoped silicon photodetectors using light-trapping strategies.
motivation: To improve the quantum efficiency of silicon photodetectors in the short-wavelength infrared range for applications like night-vision technology.
method: The authors employ a light-trapping architecture combined with Te hyperdoping to enhance absorption and carrier collection.
result: They achieve a significant increase in quantum efficiency in the short-wavelength infrared region.
conclusion: The proposed architecture could enable CMOS-compatible night-vision technology.

title: Implementation And Application Of A $\mathrm{DFT}\text{+}U\text{+}V$ Approach Within The All-electron Flapw Method
authors: W. Beida, G. Bihlmayer, C. Friedrich, G. Michalicek, D. Wortmann, And S. Blügel
abstract:

We present an implementation of the density-functional theory [MATH] formalism within the all-electron full-potential linearized augmented–plane-wave (FLAPW) method as implemented in the FLEUR code. The [MATH] formalism extends DFT, supplemented by the on-site Coulomb interac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045129] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper implements a DFT+U+V approach within the all-electron FLAPW method for improved treatment of strongly correlated materials.
motivation: Standard DFT fails to accurately describe strongly correlated systems; the DFT+U+V method adds on-site and inter-site Hubbard corrections to improve accuracy.
method: The authors implement the DFT+U+V formalism in the all-electron FLAPW code FLEUR, including the calculation of effective interaction parameters.
result: The implementation is validated on several transition metal oxides, showing improved band gaps and magnetic moments compared to standard DFT and DFT+U.
conclusion: The DFT+U+V approach within FLAPW provides a reliable and efficient method for studying strongly correlated materials.

title: Semiconductor-semimetal Transition In Van Der Waals Carbyne Crystals

method: Theoretical investigation using electronic structure calculations and comparison with photoluminescence experiments.
result: A semiconductor-semimetal transition is predicted in these carbon chain crystals.
conclusion: Carbyne crystals exhibit tunable electronic properties relevant for future nanoscale devices.

title: Computational Method To Predict Yield Strength Under Static High Pressure: Al And Ag As Prototypes

abstract:

Yield strength is used to assess nonhydrostatic conditions in diamond anvil cell experiments, serving as a critical parameter for the interpretation of high-pressure measurements. By incorporating first-principles derived high-pressure elastic properties into a thermally activated dislocation glide …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014106] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a computational method to predict yield strength of metals under high pressure using first-principles elastic properties and dislocation glide theory.
motivation: Yield strength is crucial for assessing nonhydrostatic conditions in diamond anvil cell experiments, but experimental measurement is challenging; a predictive computational method is needed.
method: First-principles calculations are used to obtain high-pressure elastic constants, which are then input into a thermally activated dislocation glide model to compute yield strength.
result: The method is applied to aluminum and silver, yielding yield strength values that agree well with available experimental data under high pressure.
conclusion: The proposed computational approach provides a reliable way to predict yield strength under static high pressure, aiding interpretation of high-pressure experiments.

title: Variational Approach To Yukawa Fluids. I. Thermodynamics

The excess energy, entropy, and pressure of a strongly coupled Yukawa fluid are calculated from the variational approach using the fluid of hard spheres as a reference system. As in the case of the one-component plasma, the Percus-Yevick virial entropy is appropriate for such calculations and delive…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015216] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a variational hard-sphere reference system to compute thermodynamic properties of Yukawa fluids.
motivation: To accurately calculate excess energy, entropy, and pressure of strongly coupled Yukawa fluids, which are important in plasma physics and soft condensed matter.
method: A variational approach with a hard-sphere reference fluid and the Percus-Yevick virial entropy is employed.
result: The method yields accurate thermodynamic functions for Yukawa fluids across a range of coupling parameters.
conclusion: The variational hard-sphere approach is effective for describing thermodynamics of Yukawa fluids, extending previous work on one-component plasmas.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.

result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
